constitution-u0a2befdebb4c29a7bc-1.text: Adopted by popular vote on 12 December 1993

constitution-u0ec370686bc2b7b448-1.text: with amendments approved in the nationwide vote

constitution-ueb1a5f90f357c9f71a-1.text: We, the multinational people of the Russian Federation,

constitution-ud8542b10e577738f13-1.text: united by a common destiny on our land,

constitution-uaac7baa1f7bf7eb614-1.text: affirming human rights and freedoms, civil peace and concord,

constitution-ub16448d57f7371d009-1.text: preserving the historically established unity of the State,

constitution-u68184a4fc69c2250d1-1.text: proceeding from the universally recognized principles of the equality and self-determination of peoples,

constitution-ue22fd7e3edcd92006f-1.text: honouring the memory of our ancestors, who passed on to us love and respect for the Fatherland and faith in goodness and justice,

constitution-ude4f7080ef725835bc-1.text: reviving Russia's sovereign statehood and affirming the inviolability of its democratic foundation,

constitution-u55baf860885b3cb247-1.text: striving to ensure Russia's well-being and prosperity,

constitution-u452f4e319962fb3461-1.text: proceeding from our responsibility for our Motherland to present and future generations,

constitution-uc8899d107e9f79d919-1.text: recognizing ourselves as part of the world community,

constitution-u6705dd206da3c424e1-1.text: adopt the CONSTITUTION OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION.

constitution-u55c6e071830b20b21e-1.text: CHAPTER 1. FOUNDATIONS OF THE CONSTITUTIONAL ORDER
constitution-u55c6e071830b20b21e-1.locator: CHAPTER 1. FOUNDATIONS OF THE CONSTITUTIONAL ORDER

constitution-u4498ed5e420844b039-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation — Russia is a democratic federal State governed by the rule of law, with a republican form of government.

constitution-u8860c11cfe4883ecdb-1.text: 2. The names Russian Federation and Russia are equivalent.

constitution-u72ee2197858cb795cd-1.text: The individual and their rights and freedoms are the highest value. Recognition, observance and protection of human and civil rights and freedoms are the duty of the State.

constitution-u780814442349094e86-1.text: 1. The bearer of sovereignty and the sole source of power in the Russian Federation is its multinational people.

constitution-ud5ee189bbc46d6d3a5-1.text: 2. The people exercise their power directly and also through bodies of state authority and local self-government bodies.

constitution-u0d1115748938afffb4-1.text: 3. The supreme direct expression of the power of the people is the referendum and free elections.

constitution-udaad3e7637f7ec3413-1.text: 4. No one may appropriate power in the Russian Federation. Seizure of power or appropriation of powers of authority is punishable under federal law.

constitution-udff000befbdabc4813-1.text: 1. The sovereignty of the Russian Federation extends throughout its territory.

constitution-ueeb0c593303e2462ca-1.text: 2. The Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal laws have supremacy throughout the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u80d8b30d4ad2484aa8-1.text: 3. The Russian Federation ensures the integrity and inviolability of its territory.

constitution-ud6b6d2144d8dadc7bc-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation consists of republics, territories, regions, cities of federal significance, an autonomous region and autonomous areas — equal constituent entities of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u6639825412ef2c0c49-1.text: 2. A republic (State) has its own constitution and legislation. A territory, region, city of federal significance, autonomous region or autonomous area has its own charter and legislation.

constitution-uda3054f17569bcb707-1.text: 3. The federal structure of the Russian Federation is based on its state integrity, the unity of the system of state authority, the delimitation of matters of jurisdiction and powers between bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities, and the equality and self-determination of peoples in the Russian Federation.

constitution-ue07e5ad1b860ca573c-1.text: 4. In their relations with federal bodies of state authority, all constituent entities of the Russian Federation are equal to one another.

constitution-u2ab80a531756159aa6-1.text: 1. Citizenship of the Russian Federation is acquired and terminated in accordance with federal law and is single and equal, irrespective of the grounds for its acquisition.

constitution-u713c174a4588751d08-1.text: 2. Every citizen of the Russian Federation possesses in its territory all rights and freedoms and bears the equal duties provided for by the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u25e643351bf1b34530-1.text: 3. A citizen of the Russian Federation may not be deprived of citizenship or of the right to change it.

constitution-u8b864da064f7c8ad2f-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation is a social State whose policy is directed towards creating conditions that ensure a dignified life and the free development of the individual.

constitution-u5f9d36c8bbd9c39b5d-1.text: 2. In the Russian Federation, people's labour and health are protected, a guaranteed minimum wage is established, state support is provided for the family, motherhood, fatherhood and childhood, persons with disabilities and older citizens, a system of social services is developed, and state pensions, benefits and other guarantees of social protection are established.

constitution-u8df179959df85494d0-1.text: 1. In the Russian Federation, the unity of the economic space, the free movement of goods, services and financial resources, support for competition and freedom of economic activity are guaranteed.

constitution-u856fa1a0886ce353c4-1.text: 2. Private, state, municipal and other forms of ownership are recognized and protected equally in the Russian Federation.

constitution-u1e7219757b09db998f-1.text: 1. Land and other natural resources are used and protected in the Russian Federation as the basis of the life and activity of the peoples living in the relevant territory.

constitution-ufabbc6cc28d760f1b6-1.text: 2. Land and other natural resources may be held in private, state, municipal and other forms of ownership.

constitution-u9a351be5af65a89019-1.text: State power in the Russian Federation is exercised on the basis of its separation into legislative, executive and judicial powers. Legislative, executive and judicial bodies are independent.

constitution-ud860b7745a34c305d7-1.text: 1. State power in the Russian Federation is exercised by the President of the Russian Federation, the Federal Assembly (the Federation Council and the State Duma), the Government of the Russian Federation and the courts of the Russian Federation.

constitution-udfa0fb4c21c8df4ad2-1.text: 2. State power in the constituent entities of the Russian Federation is exercised by the bodies of state authority established by them.

constitution-u5c7223678aa4970937-1.text: 3. Matters of jurisdiction and powers are delimited between bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities by this Constitution, the Federation Treaty and other treaties delimiting matters of jurisdiction and powers.

constitution-ud397de86ede882bb8d-1.text: Local self-government is recognized and guaranteed in the Russian Federation. Local self-government is independent within the limits of its powers. Local self-government bodies do not form part of the system of bodies of state authority.

constitution-u51f5c47d1c1020d2b2-1.text: 1. Ideological diversity is recognized in the Russian Federation.

constitution-ud3f11856c4dace79fd-1.text: 2. No ideology may be established as a state or mandatory ideology.

constitution-ud8e1aabfc6d19e6cc9-1.text: 3. Political diversity and a multiparty system are recognized in the Russian Federation.

constitution-u435289becfc2202b13-1.text: 4. Public associations are equal before the law.

constitution-uefaaacb9497247be6d-1.text: 5. The establishment and activities of public associations whose aims or actions are directed at forcibly changing the foundations of the constitutional order, violating the integrity of the Russian Federation, undermining state security, creating armed formations or inciting social, racial, ethnic or religious strife are prohibited.

constitution-u4fac86b484213b96c5-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation is a secular State. No religion may be established as a state or mandatory religion.

constitution-u961206ecbcf14e3b54-1.text: 2. Religious associations are separate from the State and equal before the law.

constitution-ue39197fbbb8a944d9b-1.text: 1. The Constitution of the Russian Federation has supreme legal force and direct effect and applies throughout the territory of the Russian Federation. Laws and other legal acts adopted in the Russian Federation must not contradict the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u80dcdae3557e55e2e7-1.text: 2. Bodies of state authority, local self-government bodies, officials, citizens and their associations are obliged to observe the Constitution of the Russian Federation and the laws.

constitution-u0fef294ef47d45beb0-1.text: 3. Laws are subject to official publication. Unpublished laws do not apply. Any normative legal acts affecting human and civil rights, freedoms and duties may not be applied unless officially published for general information.

constitution-uea03a1eec2fa881485-1.text: 4. Universally recognized principles and rules of international law and the international treaties of the Russian Federation form an integral part of its legal system. If an international treaty of the Russian Federation establishes rules different from those provided for by law, the rules of the international treaty apply.

constitution-uee3a10b6265626dc10-1.text: 1. The provisions of this chapter of the Constitution constitute the foundations of the constitutional order of the Russian Federation and may be changed only in the manner established by this Constitution.

constitution-u951dc75cfe199afcaf-1.text: 2. No other provisions of this Constitution may contradict the foundations of the constitutional order of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ua92fbd518dc5b76d76-1.text: CHAPTER 2. HUMAN AND CIVIL RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS
constitution-ua92fbd518dc5b76d76-1.locator: CHAPTER 2. HUMAN AND CIVIL RIGHTS AND FREEDOMS

constitution-ud9f585f7a895356270-1.text: 1. In the Russian Federation, human and civil rights and freedoms are recognized and guaranteed according to universally recognized principles and rules of international law and in accordance with this Constitution.

constitution-uf4d27a33eb70cb4779-1.text: 2. Fundamental human rights and freedoms are inalienable and belong to everyone from birth.

constitution-ud7aaa7d7d0d23a0c95-1.text: 3. The exercise of human and civil rights and freedoms must not violate the rights and freedoms of others.

constitution-u2c079cf4585762f1dc-1.text: Human and civil rights and freedoms have direct effect. They determine the meaning, content and application of laws, the activity of the legislative and executive authorities and local self-government, and are secured by the administration of justice.

constitution-ud6912bd1d600e3ac5b-1.text: 1. Everyone is equal before the law and the courts.

constitution-u213823fe263582937b-1.text: 2. The State guarantees equality of human and civil rights and freedoms regardless of sex, race, ethnicity, language, origin, property or official status, place of residence, attitude to religion, beliefs, membership of public associations or other circumstances. All forms of restrictions on citizens' rights on grounds of social, racial, ethnic, linguistic or religious affiliation are prohibited.

constitution-u11099d808c0b9b6131-1.text: 3. Men and women have equal rights and freedoms and equal opportunities to exercise them.

constitution-u987bd80b27318129a9-1.text: 1. Everyone has the right to life.

constitution-ud3bdeb85bd1ea397fd-1.text: 2. Until its abolition, the death penalty may be established by federal law as an exceptional punishment for particularly serious crimes against life, provided that the accused is granted the right to have their case heard by a court sitting with a jury.

constitution-u511699c8838e42f165-1.text: 1. The dignity of the individual is protected by the State. Nothing may serve as grounds for diminishing it.

constitution-u78969f58576b845e1d-1.text: 2. No one shall be subjected to torture, violence or other cruel or degrading treatment or punishment. No one may be subjected to medical, scientific or other experiments without voluntary consent.

constitution-ud3db0616a7b09dfed6-1.text: 1. Everyone has the right to liberty and personal inviolability.

constitution-u6d85dbf59d1c36d78e-1.text: 2. Arrest, remand in custody and continued detention are permitted only by a court decision. Before a court decision, a person may not be detained for more than 48 hours.

constitution-uea56f3a18df5e6ecd2-1.text: 1. Everyone has the right to the inviolability of private life, personal and family privacy, and protection of their honour and good name.

constitution-ua9c33f4156967ec4ca-1.text: 2. Everyone has the right to privacy of correspondence, telephone conversations, postal, telegraphic and other communications. This right may be restricted only on the basis of a court decision.

constitution-u2e7e56ee5dc03d7593-1.text: 1. Collecting, storing, using and disseminating information about a person's private life without their consent is not permitted.

constitution-u6a8eb5d0185dd0b1fb-1.text: 2. Bodies of state authority and local self-government bodies and their officials are obliged to ensure that everyone can inspect documents and materials directly affecting their rights and freedoms, unless otherwise provided by law.

constitution-u4b42a420b4318fceff-1.text: The home is inviolable. No one may enter a home against the will of those living there except in cases established by federal law or on the basis of a court decision.

constitution-u6eb0d1cef0206858aa-1.text: 1. Everyone is entitled to determine and indicate their ethnic affiliation. No one may be compelled to determine or indicate their ethnic affiliation.

constitution-u4de974f0335d977296-1.text: 2. Everyone has the right to use their native language and freely to choose the language of communication, upbringing, education and creative activity.

constitution-u4b3cd8dee203abd0fa-1.text: 1. Everyone lawfully present in the territory of the Russian Federation has the right to move freely and to choose their place of stay and residence.

constitution-ud44d551317669bf228-1.text: 2. Everyone may freely leave the Russian Federation. A citizen of the Russian Federation has the right to return to the Russian Federation without hindrance.

constitution-u7e1ae9d3f529048a19-1.text: Everyone is guaranteed freedom of conscience and freedom of religion, including the right to profess any religion individually or jointly with others or to profess none, freely to choose, hold and disseminate religious and other beliefs and to act in accordance with them.

constitution-uc0c41038b6f2107ff4-1.text: 1. Everyone is guaranteed freedom of thought and speech.

constitution-u3b539e8cbd5a9859a3-1.text: 2. Propaganda or agitation inciting social, racial, ethnic or religious hatred and enmity is not permitted. Propaganda of social, racial, ethnic, religious or linguistic supremacy is prohibited.

constitution-ub62c783603ec499773-1.text: 3. No one may be compelled to express their opinions and beliefs or to renounce them.

constitution-u2ecbefdc5243ab2179-1.text: 4. Everyone has the right freely to seek, receive, transmit, produce and disseminate information by any lawful means. The list of information constituting state secrets is determined by federal law.

constitution-u76122b94b69f2f7355-1.text: 5. Freedom of the mass media is guaranteed. Censorship is prohibited.

constitution-ud058613aed93085284-1.text: 1. Everyone has the right of association, including the right to establish trade unions to protect their interests. Freedom of activity of public associations is guaranteed.

constitution-uab00d1608c08491aea-1.text: 2. No one may be compelled to join or remain in any association.

constitution-u0832d9176ceb41fa3f-1.text: Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to assemble peacefully and without weapons and to hold meetings, rallies, demonstrations, marches and pickets.

constitution-u2f65d6489a4dc45b50-1.text: 1. Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to participate in administering state affairs both directly and through their representatives.

constitution-u8f3fef806d520b79b3-1.text: 2. Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to elect and be elected to bodies of state authority and local self-government bodies, and to participate in referendums.

constitution-ued0c0022c6732723c3-1.text: 3. Citizens declared legally incapable by a court, and those held in places of deprivation of liberty under a court sentence, have no right to elect or be elected.

constitution-uc85349640799d42bf7-1.text: 4. Citizens of the Russian Federation have equal access to state service.

constitution-uc70b8482ce75f7dd37-1.text: 5. Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to participate in the administration of justice.

constitution-u1ea587483f29b0a796-1.text: Citizens of the Russian Federation have the right to apply personally and to submit individual and collective appeals to state bodies and local self-government bodies.

constitution-u5b67e7d44d0824f7f3-1.text: 1. Everyone has the right freely to use their abilities and property for entrepreneurial and other economic activity not prohibited by law.

constitution-u0bbf93e7106a24e445-1.text: 2. Economic activity directed at monopolization or unfair competition is not permitted.

constitution-u819d3e9e34991bf745-1.text: 1. The right of private ownership is protected by law.

constitution-u6bfc6b75842242fafb-1.text: 2. Everyone is entitled to own property and to possess, use and dispose of it both individually and jointly with others.

constitution-ud5808db3d328a744b8-1.text: 3. No one may be deprived of their property except by a court decision. Property may be compulsorily alienated for state needs only subject to prior and equivalent compensation.

constitution-ude7a04ab171f8a3ed6-1.text: 4. The right of inheritance is guaranteed.

constitution-ub4d15f63c9d8e9fbb3-1.text: 1. Citizens and their associations are entitled to hold land in private ownership.

constitution-u4b9b0a6be3e712270a-1.text: 2. Owners freely possess, use and dispose of land and other natural resources, provided that this does not harm the environment or violate the rights and lawful interests of others.

constitution-u13bc3c316a0b6cf74d-1.text: 3. The conditions and procedure for using land are determined on the basis of federal law.

constitution-u265fb357594d2812d7-1.text: 1. Labour is free. Everyone has the right freely to dispose of their capacity for work and to choose their occupation and profession.

constitution-u3ab9aa66a3c9ef3c16-1.text: 3. Everyone has the right to work in conditions meeting safety and hygiene requirements, to remuneration for work without any discrimination and not below the minimum wage established by federal law, and to protection against unemployment.

constitution-u9948363521ab82afda-1.text: 4. The right to individual and collective labour disputes using the means of settlement established by federal law, including the right to strike, is recognized.

constitution-uaac2185754289a2050-1.text: 5. Everyone has the right to rest. Persons working under an employment contract are guaranteed the working hours, days off, public holidays and paid annual leave established by federal law.

constitution-ud6bd69a2bd8f37b927-1.text: 1. Motherhood, childhood and the family are protected by the State.

constitution-u57ec9e1a8fd63194c5-1.text: 2. Caring for and bringing up children is an equal right and duty of parents.

constitution-u93f9835d2b1707f3e3-1.text: 3. Able-bodied children who have reached 18 years of age must care for their parents who are unable to work.

constitution-u82de1986c21adf8eac-1.text: 1. Everyone is guaranteed social security in old age, in the event of illness, disability or loss of a breadwinner, for bringing up children and in other cases established by law.

constitution-u79fe76b9ae08d2e4e1-1.text: 2. State pensions and social benefits are established by law.

constitution-u59b02f140a346d692c-1.text: 3. Voluntary social insurance, the establishment of additional forms of social security and charity are encouraged.

constitution-ud6078d9e1a962a3428-1.text: 1. Everyone has the right to housing. No one may be arbitrarily deprived of housing.

constitution-u37cc440ac62471fc09-1.text: 2. Bodies of state authority and local self-government bodies encourage housing construction and create conditions for exercising the right to housing.

constitution-ud05a25171da89039a0-1.text: 3. Low-income and other citizens specified by law who need housing are provided with it free of charge or at an affordable price from state, municipal and other housing stocks, in accordance with standards established by law.

constitution-uf5e4e143dbd1f23a2d-1.text: 1. Everyone has the right to health protection and medical care. Medical care in state and municipal healthcare institutions is provided to citizens free of charge, funded by the relevant budget, insurance contributions and other revenues.

constitution-u42c4b09a4bb301f181-1.text: 2. In the Russian Federation, federal programmes to protect and improve public health are funded; measures are taken to develop state, municipal and private healthcare systems; and activities promoting human health, physical culture and sport, environmental well-being and sanitary and epidemiological well-being are encouraged.

constitution-u95584aa5225ac410d2-1.text: 3. Concealment by officials of facts and circumstances that threaten people's life and health entails liability under federal law.

constitution-u16bc9c9ab04fb612c5-1.text: Everyone has the right to a favourable environment, reliable information about its condition and compensation for harm caused to their health or property by an environmental offence.

constitution-u18919aef56780cf68b-1.text: 1. Everyone has the right to education.

constitution-uea086d7ba3e83140f7-1.text: 2. General accessibility and free provision of preschool, basic general and secondary vocational education in state or municipal educational institutions and at enterprises are guaranteed.

constitution-u8b5f16605b67ca4a10-1.text: 3. Everyone is entitled, on a competitive basis, to receive higher education free of charge in a state or municipal educational institution and at an enterprise.

constitution-ue32664de74ad9ea102-1.text: 4. Basic general education is compulsory. Parents or persons acting in their place ensure that children receive basic general education.

constitution-udb87d7258687c7a359-1.text: 5. The Russian Federation establishes federal state educational standards and supports various forms of education and self-education.

constitution-u4a0690e66a80d6e4f2-1.text: 1. Everyone is guaranteed freedom of literary, artistic, scientific, technical and other creative activity and of teaching. Intellectual property is protected by law.

constitution-ua77096eab0ffafd7c2-1.text: 2. Everyone has the right to participate in cultural life, use cultural institutions and have access to cultural assets.

constitution-u81aa91ed16b7ba4517-1.text: 3. Everyone is obliged to care for the preservation of historical and cultural heritage and to safeguard historical and cultural monuments.

constitution-ue0ab2462af48d49a50-1.text: 1. State protection of human and civil rights and freedoms in the Russian Federation is guaranteed.

constitution-u9e84023ece5baf23b1-1.text: 2. Everyone is entitled to protect their rights and freedoms by all means not prohibited by law.

constitution-u81c7b87d9ab21f6ea2-1.text: 1. Everyone is guaranteed judicial protection of their rights and freedoms.

constitution-u5663d3fbc5d2fa88be-1.text: 2. Decisions and actions (or inaction) of bodies of state authority, local self-government bodies, public associations and officials may be challenged in court.

constitution-u8c944eb2069ce4b666-1.text: 3. In accordance with international treaties of the Russian Federation, everyone is entitled to apply to intergovernmental bodies for the protection of human rights and freedoms if all available domestic legal remedies have been exhausted.

constitution-u4b48b095b1d0f8e918-1.text: 1. No one may be deprived of the right to have their case heard by the court and judge to whose jurisdiction it is assigned by law.

constitution-uddddebdcda71a2083a-1.text: 2. A person accused of a crime has the right to have their case heard by a court sitting with a jury in cases provided for by federal law.

constitution-ub3b27f8fc27f0cb05a-1.text: 1. Everyone is guaranteed the right to qualified legal assistance. Legal assistance is provided free of charge in cases prescribed by law.

constitution-uea42c5c02fa533779b-1.text: 2. Every person detained, remanded in custody or accused of a crime has the right to the assistance of a lawyer (defence counsel) from the time of detention, remand in custody or the bringing of charges, respectively.

constitution-u0e81990f13f3a6e939-1.text: 1. Everyone accused of a crime is presumed innocent until their guilt is proved in the manner prescribed by federal law and established by a court judgment that has entered into legal force.

constitution-ua866789a1d393c5c3e-1.text: 2. The accused is not obliged to prove their innocence.

constitution-ue21faf5afb8fe59e84-1.text: 3. Irremovable doubts as to a person's guilt are interpreted in favour of the accused.

constitution-u39f4842f794c980ae9-1.text: 1. No one may be convicted twice for the same crime.

constitution-u573c0470f5f2b925b5-1.text: 2. Evidence obtained in violation of federal law may not be used in the administration of justice.

constitution-u59d13587167ae41161-1.text: 3. Everyone convicted of a crime has the right to have the judgment reviewed by a higher court in the manner established by federal law and the right to request a pardon or mitigation of punishment.

constitution-ue2dcc4b458fdb29298-1.text: 1. No one is obliged to testify against themselves, their spouse or close relatives, whose scope is defined by federal law.

constitution-ufb6b1d34d20e2ced35-1.text: 2. Federal law may establish other cases of exemption from the obligation to give testimony.

constitution-u967492b56d54066f24-1.text: The rights of victims of crimes and abuses of power are protected by law. The State ensures victims' access to justice and compensation for damage caused.

constitution-ub39d0b9d4fc07926f0-1.text: Everyone has the right to compensation by the State for harm caused by unlawful actions (or inaction) of bodies of state authority or their officials.

constitution-uc8dc0dbea04212e0b5-1.text: 1. A law establishing or increasing liability has no retroactive effect.

constitution-u0a6e6b6352aff3bd6f-1.text: 2. No one may be held liable for an act that was not recognized as an offence at the time it was committed. If liability for an offence is abolished or mitigated after its commission, the new law applies.

constitution-u824aceab454a271844-1.text: 1. The enumeration of fundamental rights and freedoms in the Constitution of the Russian Federation must not be interpreted as denying or diminishing other universally recognized human and civil rights and freedoms.

constitution-ufbc4b6555db356e775-1.text: 2. Laws abolishing or diminishing human and civil rights and freedoms must not be enacted in the Russian Federation.

constitution-u4fc8c64a188758ee16-1.text: 3. Human and civil rights and freedoms may be restricted by federal law only to the extent necessary to protect the foundations of the constitutional order, morality, health and the rights and lawful interests of others, and to ensure national defence and state security.

constitution-u80be13de5737c59d9e-1.text: 1. During a state of emergency, specific restrictions on rights and freedoms may be established in accordance with federal constitutional law to ensure citizens' safety and protect the constitutional order, specifying their scope and duration.

constitution-u9d90311e5de93f6af8-1.text: 2. A state of emergency throughout the territory of the Russian Federation or in particular localities may be introduced in the circumstances and in the manner established by federal constitutional law.

constitution-u38d6b8e4a9ad502106-1.text: 3. The rights and freedoms provided for in Articles 20, 21, 23 (part 1), 24, 28, 34 (part 1), 40 (part 1) and 46–54 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation may not be restricted.

constitution-ub415e8157d24f0d5ed-1.text: Everyone is obliged to pay legally established taxes and levies. Laws introducing new taxes or worsening the position of taxpayers have no retroactive effect.

constitution-u4212084b9b10b8ada4-1.text: Everyone is obliged to preserve nature and the environment and to treat natural resources with care.

constitution-ub8ac7bf067c492b559-1.text: 1. Defence of the Fatherland is the duty and obligation of a citizen of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u6d7f3746fcf5354c60-1.text: 2. A citizen of the Russian Federation performs military service in accordance with federal law.

constitution-u3a78b54aee109edb79-1.text: 3. A citizen of the Russian Federation whose beliefs or religion conflict with military service, and in other cases established by federal law, has the right to substitute alternative civilian service for it.

constitution-ufdf74fea29768b6e57-1.text: A citizen of the Russian Federation may independently exercise their rights and duties in full from the age of 18.

constitution-ufc2a239fc0cbca2ef9-1.text: 1. A citizen of the Russian Federation may not be expelled from the Russian Federation or extradited to another State.

constitution-u8090353e3cb7e3b566-1.text: 2. The Russian Federation guarantees its citizens protection and patronage outside its borders.

constitution-ue395fe6905539c4e0a-1.text: 1. A citizen of the Russian Federation may hold citizenship of a foreign State (dual citizenship) in accordance with federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ue545d86614d70ed2c1-1.text: 2. A citizen of the Russian Federation's possession of foreign citizenship does not diminish their rights and freedoms or release them from duties arising from Russian citizenship, unless otherwise provided by federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ub0d1d55e126a2462cf-1.text: 3. Foreign citizens and stateless persons in the Russian Federation enjoy rights and bear duties on an equal footing with citizens of the Russian Federation, except in cases established by federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ubf82de7a799b1c1e1d-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation grants political asylum to foreign citizens and stateless persons in accordance with universally recognized rules of international law.

constitution-u4f88be0156d715e257-1.text: 2. The Russian Federation does not permit extradition to other States of persons persecuted for political beliefs or for actions (or inaction) not recognized as crimes in the Russian Federation. Extradition of persons accused of crimes and transfer of convicted persons to serve sentences in other States are carried out on the basis of federal law or an international treaty of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u82fced101853d48aad-1.text: The provisions of this chapter constitute the foundations of the legal status of the individual in the Russian Federation and may be changed only in the manner established by this Constitution.

constitution-u350af52807d82b5355-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation comprises the following constituent entities of the Russian Federation:

constitution-ub196f25be4dd495c98-1.text: Republic of Adygea (Adygea), Republic of Altai, Republic of Bashkortostan, Republic of Buryatia, Republic of Dagestan, Donetsk People's Republic <1>, Republic of Ingushetia <2>, Kabardino-Balkarian Republic, Republic of Kalmykia <3>, Karachay-Cherkess Republic, Republic of Karelia, Komi Republic, Republic of Crimea <4>, Lugansk People's Republic <5>, Republic of Mari El, Republic of Mordovia, Republic of Sakha (Yakutia), Republic of North Ossetia–Alania <6>, Republic of Tatarstan (Tatarstan), Republic of Tyva, Udmurt Republic, Republic of Khakassia, Chechen Republic, Chuvash Republic–Chuvashia <7>;

constitution-u6d9637e8bd211f3325-1.text: Altai Territory, Transbaikal Territory <8>, Kamchatka Territory <9>, Krasnodar Territory, Krasnoyarsk Territory <10>, Perm Territory <11>, Primorye Territory, Stavropol Territory, Khabarovsk Territory;

constitution-u595651bd3ebcea2dab-1.text: Amur Region, Arkhangelsk Region, Astrakhan Region, Belgorod Region, Bryansk Region, Vladimir Region, Volgograd Region, Vologda Region, Voronezh Region, Zaporozhye Region <12>, Ivanovo Region, Irkutsk Region <13>, Kaliningrad Region, Kaluga Region, Kemerovo Region–Kuzbass <14>, Kirov Region, Kostroma Region, Kurgan Region, Kursk Region, Leningrad Region, Lipetsk Region, Magadan Region, Moscow Region, Murmansk Region, Nizhny Novgorod Region, Novgorod Region, Novosibirsk Region, Omsk Region, Orenburg Region, Oryol Region, Penza Region, Pskov Region, Rostov Region, Ryazan Region, Samara Region, Saratov Region, Sakhalin Region, Sverdlovsk Region, Smolensk Region, Tambov Region, Tver Region, Tomsk Region, Tula Region, Tyumen Region, Ulyanovsk Region, Kherson Region <15>, Chelyabinsk Region, Yaroslavl Region;

constitution-u4b851f8e4632c95140-1.text: Moscow, Saint Petersburg and Sevastopol <16> — cities of federal significance;

constitution-u29855d73a14e683119-1.text: Nenets Autonomous Area, Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Area–Yugra <17>, Chukotka Autonomous Area, Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Area.

constitution-u0463c9f707f29fff00-1.text: 2. Admission to the Russian Federation and the formation of a new constituent entity within it are carried out in the manner established by federal constitutional law.

constitution-ue405e309d128dfd278-1.text: <1> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — the Donetsk People's Republic — is given in accordance with Federal Constitutional Law No. 5-ФКЗ of 4 October 2022, ‘On the Admission of the Donetsk People's Republic to the Russian Federation and the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity — the Donetsk People's Republic’ (Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (www.pravo.gov.ru), 2022, 5 October, No. 0001202210050005).

constitution-u7d25008ab71f5aa26e-1.text: <2> The new name of the Republic is given in accordance with Presidential Decree of the Russian Federation No. 20 of 9 January 1996, ‘On the Inclusion of New Names of Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 1996, No. 3, Art. 152).

constitution-u635a6e5c429e963afc-1.text: <3> The new name of the Republic is given in accordance with Presidential Decree of the Russian Federation No. 173 of 10 February 1996, ‘On the Inclusion of a New Name of a Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 1996, No. 7, Art. 676).

constitution-u4e7138e77ccc3947c2-1.text: <4> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — the Republic of Crimea — is given in accordance with Federal Constitutional Law No. 6-ФКЗ of 21 March 2014, ‘On the Admission of the Republic of Crimea to the Russian Federation and the Formation within the Russian Federation of New Constituent Entities — the Republic of Crimea and the City of Federal Significance Sevastopol’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2014, No. 12, Art. 1201).

constitution-u48513fbcf9ad5d307d-1.text: <5> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — the Lugansk People's Republic — is given in accordance with Federal Constitutional Law No. 6-ФКЗ of 4 October 2022, ‘On the Admission of the Lugansk People's Republic to the Russian Federation and the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity — the Lugansk People's Republic’ (Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (www.pravo.gov.ru), 2022, 5 October, No. 0001202210050006).

constitution-u44e46f374c88a2527d-1.text: <6> The new name of the Republic is given in accordance with Presidential Decree of the Russian Federation No. 20 of 9 January 1996, ‘On the Inclusion of New Names of Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 1996, No. 3, Art. 152).

constitution-uf920923b37c8b2bfad-1.text: <7> The new name of the Republic is given in accordance with Presidential Decree of the Russian Federation No. 679 of 9 June 2001, ‘On the Inclusion of a New Name of a Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2001, No. 24, Art. 2421).

constitution-ubcdea387eb78ce0e1b-1.text: <8> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — Transbaikal Territory — is given in connection with its formation from 1 March 2008, and the names of Chita Region and the Agin-Buryat Autonomous Area, which ceased to exist as constituent entities of the Russian Federation from 1 March 2008, were removed from part 1 of Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation on the basis of Federal Constitutional Law No. 5-ФКЗ of 21 July 2007, ‘On the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation as a Result of the Merger of Chita Region and the Agin-Buryat Autonomous Area’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2007, No. 30, Art. 3745).

constitution-uf8263ad845638836cb-1.text: <9> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — Kamchatka Territory — is given in connection with its formation from 1 July 2007, and the names of Kamchatka Region and the Koryak Autonomous Area, which ceased to exist as constituent entities of the Russian Federation from 1 July 2007, were removed from part 1 of Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation on the basis of Federal Constitutional Law No. 2-ФКЗ of 12 July 2006, ‘On the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation as a Result of the Merger of Kamchatka Region and the Koryak Autonomous Area’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2006, No. 29, Art. 3119).

constitution-u8381071d529b6f91d0-1.text: <10> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — Krasnoyarsk Territory — is given in connection with its formation from 1 January 2007, and the names of the Taymyr (Dolgano-Nenets) Autonomous Area and the Evenk Autonomous Area, which ceased to exist as constituent entities of the Russian Federation from 1 January 2007, were removed from part 1 of Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation on the basis of Federal Constitutional Law No. 6-ФКЗ of 14 October 2005, ‘On the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation as a Result of the Merger of Krasnoyarsk Territory, the Taymyr (Dolgano-Nenets) Autonomous Area and the Evenk Autonomous Area’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2005, No. 42, Art. 4212).

constitution-u5b1e6117ec9c25be58-1.text: <11> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — Perm Territory — is given in connection with its formation from 1 December 2005, and the names of Perm Region and the Komi-Permyak Autonomous Area, which ceased to exist as constituent entities of the Russian Federation from 1 December 2005, were removed from part 1 of Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation on the basis of Federal Constitutional Law No. 1-ФКЗ of 25 March 2004, ‘On the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation as a Result of the Merger of Perm Region and the Komi-Permyak Autonomous Area’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2004, No. 13, Art. 1110).

constitution-u500dfe6a4431bb6b71-1.text: <12> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — Zaporozhye Region — is given in accordance with Federal Constitutional Law No. 7-ФКЗ of 4 October 2022, ‘On the Admission of Zaporozhye Region to the Russian Federation and the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity — Zaporozhye Region’ (Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (www.pravo.gov.ru), 2022, 5 October, No. 0001202210050007).

constitution-ue3065c057f6f59bd6e-1.text: <13> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — Irkutsk Region — is given in connection with its formation from 1 January 2008, and the name of the Ust-Orda Buryat Autonomous Area, which ceased to exist as a constituent entity of the Russian Federation from 1 January 2008, was removed from part 1 of Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation on the basis of Federal Constitutional Law No. 6-ФКЗ of 30 December 2006, ‘On the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation as a Result of the Merger of Irkutsk Region and the Ust-Orda Buryat Autonomous Area’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2007, No. 1, Art. 1).

constitution-ue4ae0f04299f79f070-1.text: <14> The new name of the Region is given in accordance with Presidential Decree of the Russian Federation No. 130 of 27 March 2019, ‘On the Inclusion of a New Name of a Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2019, No. 13, Art. 1390).

constitution-uf55fccf11167395a2c-1.text: <15> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — Kherson Region — is given in accordance with Federal Constitutional Law No. 8-ФКЗ of 4 October 2022, ‘On the Admission of Kherson Region to the Russian Federation and the Formation within the Russian Federation of a New Constituent Entity — Kherson Region’ (Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (www.pravo.gov.ru), 2022, 5 October, No. 0001202210050008).

constitution-u19eb72433bc082e156-1.text: <16> The name of the new constituent entity of the Russian Federation — the city of federal significance Sevastopol — is given in accordance with Federal Constitutional Law No. 6-ФКЗ of 21 March 2014, ‘On the Admission of the Republic of Crimea to the Russian Federation and the Formation within the Russian Federation of New Constituent Entities — the Republic of Crimea and the City of Federal Significance Sevastopol’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2014, No. 12, Art. 1201).

constitution-u5ce896fba06b7680e2-1.text: <17> The new name of the Autonomous Area is given in accordance with Presidential Decree of the Russian Federation No. 841 of 25 July 2003, ‘On the Inclusion of a New Name of a Constituent Entity of the Russian Federation in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation’ (Collected Legislation of the Russian Federation, 2003, No. 30, Art. 3051).

constitution-u7b19ca543b72db1133-1.text: 1. The status of a republic is determined by the Constitution of the Russian Federation and the constitution of the republic.

constitution-u7518fd406b6b9cf5f3-1.text: 2. The status of a territory, region, city of federal significance, autonomous region or autonomous area is determined by the Constitution of the Russian Federation and the charter of the territory, region, city of federal significance, autonomous region or autonomous area, adopted by the legislative (representative) body of the relevant constituent entity of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ub45f131a585dfbaa52-1.text: 3. Upon a submission by the legislative and executive bodies of an autonomous region or autonomous area, a federal law on that autonomous region or autonomous area may be adopted.

constitution-u44088c246bfa17d605-1.text: 4. The relations of autonomous areas forming part of a territory or region may be regulated by federal law and a treaty between the bodies of state authority of the autonomous area and, respectively, the bodies of state authority of the territory or region.

constitution-u98c9ffc4b8c01b0a16-1.text: 5. The status of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation may be changed by mutual agreement of the Russian Federation and that constituent entity in accordance with federal constitutional law.

constitution-u56e4451a4891a53132-1.text: 1. The territory of the Russian Federation includes the territories of its constituent entities, inland waters and the territorial sea, and the airspace above them. Federal territories may be established within the territory of the Russian Federation in accordance with federal law. The organization of public authority in federal territories is established by that federal law.

constitution-u6176ff040c1496b9e9-1.text: 2. The Russian Federation possesses sovereign rights and exercises jurisdiction over the continental shelf and the exclusive economic zone of the Russian Federation in the manner determined by federal law and rules of international law.

constitution-u2c2faf59098891cb76-1.text: 2.1. The Russian Federation ensures the protection of its sovereignty and territorial integrity. Actions aimed at alienating part of the territory of the Russian Federation (except delimitation, demarcation and redemarcation of the state border of the Russian Federation with neighbouring States), and calls for such actions, are not permitted.

constitution-u4f51eb76c9c1054874-1.text: 3. Boundaries between constituent entities of the Russian Federation may be changed by their mutual agreement.

constitution-u96d71e266df137aec1-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation is the legal successor of the USSR in its territory and also the legal successor (continuing State) of the USSR in respect of membership of international organizations and their bodies, participation in international treaties, and obligations and assets of the USSR outside the territory of the Russian Federation provided for by international treaties.

constitution-u49c52572976b1df4bd-1.text: 2. The Russian Federation, united by a thousand-year history, preserving the memory of ancestors who passed on to us ideals and faith in God, and continuity in the development of the Russian State, recognizes the historically established unity of the State.

constitution-u1c0c0a10591b8c4415-1.text: 3. The Russian Federation honours the memory of defenders of the Fatherland and ensures the protection of historical truth. Diminishing the significance of the people's heroic achievement in defending the Fatherland is not permitted.

constitution-ucf829c8ad2ffbcca38-1.text: 4. Children are the foremost priority of Russia's state policy. The State creates conditions conducive to children's comprehensive spiritual, moral, intellectual and physical development and to fostering patriotism, civic responsibility and respect for elders in them. While ensuring the priority of family upbringing, the State assumes parental duties towards children left without care.

constitution-u417d7550c78cad4b5a-1.text: 1. The state language of the Russian Federation throughout its territory is Russian, as the language of the state-forming people, which forms part of the multinational union of equal peoples of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u8cc550f95f8b9f28dc-1.text: 2. Republics are entitled to establish their own state languages. In bodies of state authority, local self-government bodies and state institutions of the republics, these languages are used alongside the state language of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u28b92989a0a6da2bea-1.text: 3. The Russian Federation guarantees all its peoples the right to preserve their native language and the creation of conditions for its study and development.

constitution-u41f6db302e1fd0648b-1.text: 4. Culture in the Russian Federation is the unique heritage of its multinational people. Culture is supported and protected by the State.

constitution-u2632ce80a3cda3e07d-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation guarantees the rights of indigenous small-numbered peoples in accordance with universally recognized principles and rules of international law and international treaties of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u2ebf2458a055d5cc10-1.text: 2. The State protects the cultural identity of all peoples and ethnic communities of the Russian Federation and guarantees the preservation of ethnocultural and linguistic diversity.

constitution-ua25b187368694afa93-1.text: 3. The Russian Federation supports compatriots living abroad in exercising their rights, securing protection of their interests and preserving their shared Russian cultural identity.

constitution-u7d77c39b290cc29587-1.text: 1. The state flag, coat of arms and anthem of the Russian Federation, their description and the procedure for their official use are established by federal constitutional law.

constitution-u183aff4f741d199606-1.text: 2. The capital of the Russian Federation is the city of Moscow. The status of the capital is established by federal law. Individual federal bodies of state authority may have their permanent seat in another city designated by federal constitutional law.

constitution-u489880c7bcbbecde01-1.text: The Russian Federation has jurisdiction over:

constitution-u8dab64830192813a29-1.text: а) adoption and amendment of the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal laws, and supervision of their observance;

constitution-u5dbf74382025d3d7b8-1.text: б) the federal structure and territory of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u3b679e7c01dd222b50-1.text: в) regulation and protection of human and civil rights and freedoms; citizenship in the Russian Federation; regulation and protection of the rights of ethnic minorities;

constitution-u8f28f3b94df5a83606-1.text: г) organization of public authority; establishment of the system of federal legislative, executive and judicial bodies and the procedure for their organization and activity; formation of federal bodies of state authority;

constitution-u2f0a02a72a5acf938d-1.text: д) federal state property and its management;

constitution-u66cf2e002704300ee2-1.text: е) establishment of the foundations of federal policy and federal programmes in the fields of state, economic, environmental, scientific and technological, social, cultural and national development of the Russian Federation; establishment of unified legal foundations for healthcare and upbringing and education systems, including continuing education;

constitution-u0a2cd73a33310a4cad-1.text: ж) establishment of the legal foundations of a single market; financial, currency, credit and customs regulation, currency issuance and the foundations of pricing policy; federal economic services, including federal banks;

constitution-u07fc4f0e1066941401-1.text: з) the federal budget; federal taxes and levies; federal regional development funds;

constitution-u9d4e6f2905f0cadf66-1.text: и) federal energy systems, nuclear energy and fissile materials; federal transport, transport routes, information, information technologies and communications; space activities;

constitution-u72bdaca17d92f0d415-1.text: к) foreign policy and international relations of the Russian Federation and international treaties of the Russian Federation; issues of war and peace;

constitution-udd87509475ab69fe27-1.text: л) foreign economic relations of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ue2f7fb0e47aa48dd6a-1.text: м) defence and security; defence production; determination of the procedure for selling and purchasing weapons, ammunition, military equipment and other military property; production of toxic substances and narcotic drugs and the procedure for their use; ensuring the security of the individual, society and the State in the use of information technologies and the circulation of digital data;

constitution-u0c6b5ee17671c6215b-1.text: н) determination of the status and protection of the state border, territorial sea, airspace, exclusive economic zone and continental shelf of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ufe3cedd6acabca1e71-1.text: о) the court system; the procuracy; criminal and penal enforcement legislation; amnesty and pardon; civil legislation; procedural legislation; legal regulation of intellectual property <18>;

constitution-u06ff3742d8248c0746-1.text: р) metrological services, standards, measurement standards, the metric system and time reckoning; geodesy and cartography; names of geographical features; meteorological services; official statistical and accounting records;

constitution-u05134cf82f25d8b9e2-1.text: с) state awards and honorary titles of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ua7588a5da1f9e3bd23-1.text: т) federal state service; establishment of restrictions on holding state and municipal offices and positions in state and municipal service, including restrictions connected with foreign citizenship or a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State, and restrictions connected with opening or holding accounts (deposits) and keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u3cdbd432f03845480d-1.text: <18> Point ‘о’ is reproduced as amended by the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 2-ФКЗ of 5 February 2014, ‘On the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation and the Procuracy of the Russian Federation’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 6 February 2014 (Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (www.pravo.gov.ru), 2014, 6 February, No. 0001201402060001).

constitution-u5572436b34aa3ca689-1.text: 1. The Russian Federation and the constituent entities of the Russian Federation have joint jurisdiction over:

constitution-u7efcdacb283482cf4f-1.text: а) ensuring that the constitutions and laws of republics and the charters, laws and other normative legal acts of territories, regions, cities of federal significance, the autonomous region and autonomous areas conform to the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal laws;

constitution-u64309b24850a99dfb9-1.text: б) protection of human and civil rights and freedoms; protection of the rights of ethnic minorities; ensuring legality, law and order, and public safety; the regime of border zones;

constitution-uebf637547d099f1dcf-1.text: в) matters of possession, use and disposal of land, subsoil, water and other natural resources;

constitution-u675826b6e398838c58-1.text: д) use of natural resources; agriculture; environmental protection and ensuring environmental safety; specially protected natural areas; protection of historical and cultural monuments;

constitution-u417e49190a55df0aa9-1.text: е) general matters of upbringing, education, science, culture, physical culture and sport, and youth policy;

constitution-uad6163f083dbda0722-1.text: ж) coordination of healthcare matters, including ensuring accessible and high-quality medical care, preserving and improving public health, creating conditions for healthy lifestyles and for developing a culture of responsible attitudes by citizens towards their health; social protection, including social security;

constitution-u5e654ab12f0216232d-1.text: ж.1) protection of the family, motherhood, fatherhood and childhood; protection of the institution of marriage as a union of a man and a woman; creating conditions for the proper upbringing of children in the family and for adult children to fulfil their duty to care for their parents;

constitution-uba1dba2d3a6c949975-1.text: з) implementing measures to combat disasters, natural calamities and epidemics and to eliminate their consequences;

constitution-u80933ff8eec3bb5990-1.text: и) establishment of general principles of taxation and levies in the Russian Federation;

constitution-uf85aa572ab4502adc3-1.text: к) administrative, administrative procedural, labour, family, housing, land, water and forest legislation, and legislation on subsoil and environmental protection;

constitution-u109cee0e55255131f0-1.text: л) personnel of judicial and law-enforcement bodies; the bar and the notariat;

constitution-uaa3907b78f623b786e-1.text: м) protection of the traditional habitat and way of life of small-numbered ethnic communities;

constitution-u9614403fe54245e452-1.text: н) establishment of general principles for organizing the system of bodies of state authority and local self-government;

constitution-ue48f812d5358292b4f-1.text: о) coordination of the international and foreign economic relations of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and implementation of international treaties of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u1f31b4563fe6966ac2-1.text: 2. The provisions of this Article apply equally to republics, territories, regions, cities of federal significance, the autonomous region and autonomous areas.

constitution-u23d5c24c16b395a046-1.text: Outside the jurisdiction of the Russian Federation and its powers in matters of joint jurisdiction of the Russian Federation and its constituent entities, the constituent entities of the Russian Federation possess the full extent of state power.

constitution-u0ea68d3db452520e94-1.text: 1. Customs boundaries, duties, levies or any other obstacles to the free movement of goods, services and financial resources may not be established within the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u0eeafc545d060fe98a-1.text: 2. Restrictions on the movement of goods and services may be introduced in accordance with federal law if necessary to ensure security, protect people's life and health, or protect nature and cultural assets.

constitution-ud405a473a2e3d923ec-1.text: 1. The monetary unit of the Russian Federation is the rouble. Currency is issued exclusively by the Central Bank of the Russian Federation. The introduction and issuance of other currencies in the Russian Federation are not permitted.

constitution-u1b11e480609f69c0ff-1.text: 2. Protecting and ensuring the stability of the rouble is the principal function of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, which it performs independently of other bodies of state authority.

constitution-u109de4599db74cd9f9-1.text: 3. The system of taxes levied for the federal budget and the general principles of taxation and levies in the Russian Federation are established by federal law.

constitution-u9e198cddd46eab69e1-1.text: 4. State loans are issued in the manner determined by federal law and subscribed to on a voluntary basis.

constitution-u3ba9c88ca5abd621f3-1.text: 5. The Russian Federation respects citizens' labour and ensures protection of their rights. The State guarantees a minimum wage not lower than the subsistence minimum for the working-age population of the Russian Federation as a whole.

constitution-ue3df633a08c9581fd1-1.text: 6. In the Russian Federation, a pension system for citizens is formed on the principles of universality, fairness and solidarity between generations, and its effective functioning is maintained; pensions are also indexed at least once a year in the manner established by federal law.

constitution-u317f5c1bb72b8bed19-1.text: 7. In the Russian Federation, compulsory social insurance, targeted social support for citizens, and indexation of social benefits and other social payments are guaranteed in accordance with federal law.

constitution-u5e11f4bc90da07be29-1.text: In the Russian Federation, conditions are created for sustainable national economic growth, improvement of citizens' well-being and mutual trust between the State and society; protection of citizens' dignity and respect for working people are guaranteed; and a balance of citizens' rights and duties, social partnership, and economic, political and social solidarity are ensured.

constitution-uc222e846d42f465edf-1.text: 1. Federal constitutional laws and federal laws having direct effect throughout the territory of the Russian Federation are adopted on matters within the jurisdiction of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u5c21eb4cb0d43b8784-1.text: 2. On matters of joint jurisdiction of the Russian Federation and its constituent entities, federal laws are enacted, and laws and other normative legal acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation are adopted in accordance with them.

constitution-u079e8c22b2722e4c0f-1.text: 3. Federal laws may not contradict federal constitutional laws.

constitution-u206c898d4ba60528e9-1.text: 4. Outside the jurisdiction of the Russian Federation and the joint jurisdiction of the Russian Federation and its constituent entities, republics, territories, regions, cities of federal significance, the autonomous region and autonomous areas exercise their own legal regulation, including adopting laws and other normative legal acts.

constitution-u3e8a366a8f489ffe01-1.text: 5. Laws and other normative legal acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation may not contradict federal laws adopted in accordance with parts one and two of this Article. In the event of a conflict between a federal law and another act issued in the Russian Federation, the federal law applies.

constitution-u8c56a8cc3ac822d2c5-1.text: 6. In the event of a conflict between a federal law and a normative legal act of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation issued in accordance with part four of this Article, the normative legal act of the constituent entity applies.

constitution-u111b75c072c4b6fe59-1.text: 1. The system of bodies of state authority of republics, territories, regions, cities of federal significance, the autonomous region and autonomous areas is established independently by constituent entities of the Russian Federation in accordance with the foundations of the constitutional order of the Russian Federation and the general principles for organizing representative and executive bodies of state authority established by federal law.

constitution-ue15963f7e4ad41fccf-1.text: 2. Within the jurisdiction of the Russian Federation and its powers on matters of joint jurisdiction of the Russian Federation and its constituent entities, federal executive bodies and executive bodies of the constituent entities form a unified system of executive authority in the Russian Federation.

constitution-u02620782cdf46e4f5b-1.text: 3. The highest official of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation (the head of its highest executive body of state authority) may be a citizen of the Russian Federation who has reached 30 years of age, permanently resides in the Russian Federation and holds neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, the highest official of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation (the head of its highest executive body of state authority) is prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation. Federal law may establish additional requirements for the highest official of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation (the head of its highest executive body of state authority).

constitution-u290d9aa7da06339678-1.text: 1. Federal executive bodies may establish their own territorial bodies and appoint the relevant officials to exercise their powers.

constitution-u33abe3a4975f6018bf-1.text: 2. By agreement with executive bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, federal executive bodies may transfer to them the exercise of some of their powers, provided that this does not contradict the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal laws.

constitution-u0f7a59d7bfe288846e-1.text: 3. Executive bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation may, by agreement with federal executive bodies, transfer to them the exercise of some of their powers.

constitution-u03ef1b8a569714f3a9-1.text: 4. The President of the Russian Federation and the Government of the Russian Federation ensure, in accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, the exercise of the powers of federal state authority throughout the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u717dea0b1f1d21daba-1.text: 5. The head of a federal state body may be a citizen of the Russian Federation who has reached 30 years of age and holds neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, the head of a federal state body is prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u64a4b965bb38e78b5c-1.text: The Russian Federation may participate in interstate associations and transfer some of its powers to them in accordance with international treaties of the Russian Federation, provided that this does not restrict human and civil rights and freedoms or contradict the foundations of the constitutional order of the Russian Federation. Decisions of interstate bodies adopted on the basis of provisions of international treaties of the Russian Federation interpreted in a manner contrary to the Constitution of the Russian Federation are not enforceable in the Russian Federation.

constitution-uc2c88a493da82b2f65-1.text: The Russian Federation takes measures to maintain and strengthen international peace and security, ensure the peaceful coexistence of States and peoples and prevent interference in a State's internal affairs.

constitution-u7348950e69e05cfbc0-1.text: CHAPTER 4. PRESIDENT OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION
constitution-u7348950e69e05cfbc0-1.locator: CHAPTER 4. PRESIDENT OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION

constitution-u356f2fc08cfdf5fb9b-1.text: 1. The President of the Russian Federation is the head of State.

constitution-u05655d51bcde038fc6-1.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation is the guarantor of the Constitution of the Russian Federation and of human and civil rights and freedoms. In the manner established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation, the President takes measures to protect the sovereignty, independence and state integrity of the Russian Federation, maintains civil peace and concord in the country and ensures the coordinated functioning and interaction of bodies forming part of the unified system of public authority.

constitution-u23fc9d80f394bb3b9d-1.text: 3. In accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal laws, the President of the Russian Federation determines the main directions of the State's domestic and foreign policy.

constitution-uf327f1db9465c5cea3-1.text: 4. As head of State, the President of the Russian Federation represents the Russian Federation within the country and in international relations.

constitution-u21ab10039ffaa89c2f-1.text: 1. The President of the Russian Federation is elected for a term of six years by citizens of the Russian Federation on the basis of universal, equal and direct suffrage by secret ballot.

constitution-u2d0e01100dd715e207-1.text: 2. A citizen of the Russian Federation aged at least 35, who has permanently resided in the Russian Federation for at least 25 years and does not hold, and has never held, foreign citizenship or a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State, may be elected President of the Russian Federation. The requirement concerning the absence of foreign citizenship for a candidate for President of the Russian Federation does not apply to citizens of the Russian Federation who previously held citizenship of a State that, or part of which, was admitted to the Russian Federation under federal constitutional law and who permanently resided in the territory of the State or part of the State admitted to the Russian Federation. In the manner established by federal law, the President of the Russian Federation is prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u6a84430a6e7c1941d9-1.text: 3. The same person may not hold the office of President of the Russian Federation for more than two terms.

constitution-uc49cfdfd7aa9c0f393-1.text: 3.1. The provision of part 3 of Article 81 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation limiting the number of terms during which the same person may hold the office of President of the Russian Federation applies to a person who has held and/or holds that office without taking into account the number of terms for which that person has held and/or holds it at the time the constitutional amendment introducing the corresponding limitation enters into force, and does not exclude that person's possibility of holding the office of President of the Russian Federation for the terms permitted by that provision.

constitution-u73029e62b0e2aff988-1.text: 4. The procedure for electing the President of the Russian Federation is determined by federal law.

constitution-ufcebaee6ac3a4191fc-1.text: 1. On taking office, the President of the Russian Federation takes the following oath to the people:

constitution-uc50756453d30846bde-1.text: ‘In exercising the powers of President of the Russian Federation, I swear to respect and protect human and civil rights and freedoms, observe and defend the Constitution of the Russian Federation, defend the sovereignty and independence, security and integrity of the State, and faithfully serve the people.’

constitution-u42469d3ce82c0788cf-1.text: 2. The oath is taken in a solemn ceremony in the presence of senators of the Russian Federation, deputies of the State Duma and judges of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u00c2638b29e70f2411-1.text: The President of the Russian Federation:

constitution-u79aa4edf8e7cc7f95c-1.text: а) appoints the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, whose candidacy has been approved by the State Duma on the President's submission, and removes the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation from office;

constitution-u00415426e5324ad09b-1.text: б) exercises overall direction of the Government of the Russian Federation; may chair meetings of the Government of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ud35763235d8472a7fb-1.text: б.1) approves, on the proposal of the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, the structure of federal executive bodies and makes changes to it; within that structure, determines the bodies whose activities are directed by the President of the Russian Federation and those directed by the Government of the Russian Federation. If the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation is removed from office by the President of the Russian Federation, the newly appointed Chairman does not submit proposals on the structure of federal executive bodies to the President;

constitution-u7fd853ca1e0b25dccc-1.text: в) decides on the resignation of the Government of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ubc6bc6f06500bed8c5-1.text: в.1) accepts the resignation of the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation, federal ministers and heads of federal executive bodies whose activities are directed by the President of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u0428176e852d97bb36-1.text: г) submits to the State Duma a candidate for appointment as Chairman of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation; raises before the State Duma the question of removing the Chairman of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation from office;

constitution-uc50c3b5be35e00af63-1.text: д) appoints Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers whose candidacies have been approved by the State Duma (except the federal ministers referred to in point ‘д.1’ of this Article), and removes them from office;

constitution-u6be92415760a286217-1.text: д.1) appoints, after consultations with the Federation Council, and removes from office heads of federal executive bodies (including federal ministers) responsible for defence, state security, internal affairs, justice, foreign affairs, prevention of emergencies and elimination of the consequences of natural disasters, and public safety;

constitution-ufb3dd9b0fa15551450-1.text: е) submits to the Federation Council candidates for appointment as Chairman, Deputy Chairman and judges of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation, and Chairman, Deputy Chairmen and judges of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation; appoints chairmen, deputy chairmen and judges of other federal courts;

constitution-u0e1f49dc1e8bcbe26e-1.text: е.1) appoints, after consultations with the Federation Council, and removes from office the Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation, Deputy Prosecutors General of the Russian Federation, prosecutors of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and prosecutors of military and other specialized procuracies equivalent to prosecutors of constituent entities; appoints and removes from office other prosecutors for whom federal law establishes this procedure of appointment and removal;

constitution-u96dd5c237bd92ab22c-1.text: е.2) appoints and removes representatives of the Russian Federation in the Federation Council <19>;

constitution-u84d11adc600d237b69-1.text: е.3) submits to the Federation Council a proposal to terminate, in accordance with federal constitutional law, the powers of the Chairman, Deputy Chairman and judges of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation, the Chairman, Deputy Chairmen and judges of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, and the chairmen, deputy chairmen and judges of cassation and appellate courts, if they commit an act disgracing a judge's honour and dignity, or in other cases provided for by federal constitutional law indicating that a judge is unable to exercise their powers;

constitution-uf542f8b264cd19b993-1.text: е.4) submits to the Federation Council candidates for appointment as Chairman of the Accounts Chamber and half of its total number of auditors; submits to the State Duma candidates for appointment as Deputy Chairman of the Accounts Chamber and half of its total number of auditors;

constitution-u77c73f09a3ba32120b-1.text: е.5) forms the State Council of the Russian Federation to ensure coordinated functioning and interaction of public authorities, determine the main directions of the domestic and foreign policy of the Russian Federation and the priority directions of the State's socioeconomic development; the status of the State Council of the Russian Federation is determined by federal law;

constitution-uf045b6ed0210664675-1.text: ж) forms the Security Council of the Russian Federation to assist the head of State in exercising powers concerning national interests and the security of the individual, society and the State, maintaining civil peace and concord in the country, protecting the sovereignty, independence and state integrity of the Russian Federation, and preventing internal and external threats; heads the Security Council of the Russian Federation. The status of the Security Council of the Russian Federation is determined by federal law;

constitution-udcde3eb31d3da1e3fe-1.text: з) approves the military doctrine of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u7604ba9a8d6ccc7837-1.text: и) forms the Administration of the President of the Russian Federation to support the exercise of the President's powers;

constitution-u3f8a15cd41ff22126c-1.text: к) appoints and removes plenipotentiary representatives of the President of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u1b9bc345532b65f741-1.text: л) appoints and removes the high command of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation;

constitution-uf41a8ed2bf2208235e-1.text: м) appoints and recalls diplomatic representatives of the Russian Federation to foreign States and international organizations after consultations with the relevant committees or commissions of the chambers of the Federal Assembly.

constitution-u40e050b64cef16015c-1.text: <19> Article 83 was supplemented with point ‘е.2’ in accordance with the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 11-ФКЗ of 21 July 2014, ‘On the Federation Council of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 22 July 2014 (Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (www.pravo.gov.ru), 2014, 22 July, No. 0001201407220002).

constitution-u00c2638b29e70f2411-2.text: The President of the Russian Federation:

constitution-u2ef185c79db312287e-1.text: а) calls elections to the State Duma in accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal law;

constitution-u8727c3ef2dd4e8cca4-1.text: б) dissolves the State Duma in the cases and in the manner provided for by the Constitution of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u6c63eb5b82d172599a-1.text: в) calls a referendum in the manner established by federal constitutional law;

constitution-u822d73e9996e59866b-1.text: г) submits bills to the State Duma;

constitution-uf34ef4831ae337d9ae-1.text: д) signs and promulgates federal laws;

constitution-ud7ebc5e0c530bf79d7-1.text: е) addresses the Federal Assembly with annual messages on the situation in the country and the main directions of the State's domestic and foreign policy.

constitution-u649d49eec0f5909b26-1.text: 1. The President of the Russian Federation may use conciliation procedures to resolve disagreements between bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities, and between bodies of state authority of constituent entities of the Russian Federation. If an agreed solution is not reached, the President may refer the dispute for resolution to the appropriate court.

constitution-ub778517c442ab4e94b-1.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation is entitled to suspend acts of executive bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation if those acts contradict the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws or the international obligations of the Russian Federation, or violate human and civil rights and freedoms, pending a decision on the matter by the appropriate court.

constitution-u00c2638b29e70f2411-3.text: The President of the Russian Federation:

constitution-u1565c2a078aca3ed0e-1.text: а) directs the foreign policy of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ub2cf10fee97107b9d4-1.text: б) conducts negotiations and signs international treaties of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u7c7ad2a6a30810c738-1.text: г) receives the letters of credence and recall of diplomatic representatives accredited to the President.
