constitution-u6e25ef2fdb82616c81-1.text: 1. The President of the Russian Federation is Supreme Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ud604ed891ccd03e62a-1.text: 2. In the event of aggression against the Russian Federation or an immediate threat of aggression, the President of the Russian Federation introduces martial law throughout the territory of the Russian Federation or in particular localities, immediately informing the Federation Council and the State Duma.

constitution-u48a9080015ba8fd984-1.text: 3. The regime of martial law is determined by federal constitutional law.

constitution-uf143c8e54cdbf66c37-1.text: In the circumstances and in the manner provided for by federal constitutional law, the President of the Russian Federation introduces a state of emergency throughout the territory of the Russian Federation or in particular localities, immediately informing the Federation Council and the State Duma.

constitution-u00c2638b29e70f2411-4.text: The President of the Russian Federation:

constitution-u19848f039910faea89-1.text: а) decides matters of citizenship of the Russian Federation and the granting of political asylum;

constitution-u1ab21370efec2f00e9-1.text: б) confers state awards of the Russian Federation, honorary titles of the Russian Federation, and the highest military and special ranks;

constitution-u50eda76f8dbbf725e5-1.text: 1. The President of the Russian Federation issues decrees and executive orders.

constitution-ueaa3f860d1c15e69f2-1.text: 2. Decrees and executive orders of the President of the Russian Federation are binding throughout the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ucdc208731f6c976019-1.text: 3. Decrees and executive orders of the President of the Russian Federation must not contradict the Constitution of the Russian Federation or federal laws.

constitution-u1432f2406287af27d7-1.text: The President of the Russian Federation enjoys immunity.

constitution-ub16e3a979909289590-1.text: 1. The President of the Russian Federation begins exercising powers upon taking the oath and ceases exercising them at the expiry of the term of office, when the newly elected President of the Russian Federation takes the oath.

constitution-u54d0efdea25c942722-1.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation ceases exercising powers before the expiry of the term in the event of resignation, persistent inability for health reasons to exercise the powers vested in the President, or removal from office. In that event, the election of the President of the Russian Federation must take place no later than three months after the early termination of the exercise of powers.

constitution-uf1518e5a3caa5e5c9c-1.text: 3. Whenever the President of the Russian Federation is unable to perform the duties of office, they are temporarily performed by the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation. The Acting President of the Russian Federation has no right to dissolve the State Duma, call a referendum or submit proposals to amend or revise provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-udaac83be79f939a2df-1.text: 1. A President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers because of the expiry of the term of office, or prematurely because of resignation or persistent inability for health reasons to exercise the powers vested in the President, enjoys immunity.

constitution-u06d319fdc0010d012e-1.text: 2. Other guarantees for a President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers because of the expiry of the term of office, or prematurely because of resignation or persistent inability for health reasons to exercise the powers vested in the President, are established by federal law.

constitution-ubdeb573cfd48ce494c-1.text: 3. A President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers may be deprived of immunity in the manner provided for by Article 93 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u43dc268693e210aa5e-1.text: 1. The President of the Russian Federation may be removed from office, and a President who has ceased exercising powers may be deprived of immunity, by the Federation Council only on the basis of a charge of high treason or commission of another serious crime brought by the State Duma, confirmed by an opinion of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation that the actions of the incumbent or former President contain elements of a crime, and by an opinion of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation that the prescribed procedure for bringing the charge has been observed.

constitution-ue58bbf9e095288fcdd-1.text: 2. The State Duma's decision to bring a charge and the Federation Council's decision to remove the President of the Russian Federation from office or deprive a former President of immunity must be adopted by votes of two-thirds of the total membership of the respective chambers — senators of the Russian Federation and deputies of the State Duma — on the initiative of at least one-third of the deputies of the State Duma and with an opinion from a special commission established by the State Duma.

constitution-u84fd7f1410ca07928d-1.text: 3. The Federation Council's decision to remove the President of the Russian Federation from office or deprive a former President of immunity must be adopted no later than three months after the State Duma brings a charge against the President. If the Federation Council does not adopt a decision within that period, the charge against the incumbent or former President of the Russian Federation is deemed rejected.

constitution-u6d814d46bbb9bdd566-1.text: The Federal Assembly — the parliament of the Russian Federation — is the representative and legislative body of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u0ab1257fdfeb055c9a-1.text: 1. The Federal Assembly consists of two chambers — the Federation Council and the State Duma.

constitution-u9a20c8d03d040676ad-1.text: 2. The Federation Council consists of senators of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u93b27088b417076be4-1.text: а) two representatives from each constituent entity of the Russian Federation, one from its legislative (representative) and one from its executive body of state authority, for the term of the respective body;

constitution-u89337954403a340a9a-1.text: б) a President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers because of the expiry of the term of office or prematurely because of resignation, for life. Such a former President of the Russian Federation is entitled to decline the powers of a senator of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u5974b0a56f4da1bf94-1.text: в) no more than 30 representatives of the Russian Federation appointed by the President of the Russian Federation, of whom no more than seven may be appointed for life.

constitution-uf1fc15340b3b49fa07-1.text: 3. The total number of senators of the Russian Federation is determined by the number of representatives from the constituent entities of the Russian Federation listed in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation and the number of persons exercising the powers of senators of the Russian Federation referred to in points ‘б’ and ‘в’ of part 2 of this Article.

constitution-u9560c29c4c90d5e6e5-1.text: 4. A senator of the Russian Federation may be a citizen of the Russian Federation who has reached 30 years of age, permanently resides in the Russian Federation and holds neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, senators of the Russian Federation are prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ua615b6ddb5c82d54ac-1.text: 5. Citizens with outstanding services to the country in state and public activity may be appointed representatives of the Russian Federation in the Federation Council exercising the powers of senators of the Russian Federation for life.

constitution-u1b02f6f4c4e1b45b8c-1.text: 6. Representatives of the Russian Federation in the Federation Council, except those exercising the powers of senators of the Russian Federation for life, are appointed for a term of six years.

constitution-u387e9cf3e3de0c6bf6-1.text: 7. The State Duma consists of 450 deputies.

constitution-u9f0591e421098544ac-1.text: 1. The State Duma is elected for a term of five years <20>.

constitution-u7291a64223df0911ce-1.text: 2. The procedure for forming the Federation Council and the procedure for electing deputies of the State Duma are established by federal laws.

constitution-u8aa0ebf76493a8431e-1.text: <20> Part 1 is reproduced as amended by the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 6-ФКЗ of 30 December 2008, ‘On Changing the Terms of Office of the President of the Russian Federation and the State Duma’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 31 December 2008 (Rossiyskaya Gazeta, 2008, 31 December). It applies to a State Duma elected after the entry into force of that Law.

constitution-u7cd2e8520824f43604-1.text: 1. A citizen of the Russian Federation who has reached 21 years of age, is entitled to participate in elections, permanently resides in the Russian Federation and holds neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State may be elected a deputy of the State Duma. In the manner established by federal law, deputies of the State Duma are prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ue01d8f4610ac45188d-1.text: 2. The same person may not simultaneously be a senator of the Russian Federation and a deputy of the State Duma. A deputy of the State Duma may not be a deputy of other representative bodies of state authority or local self-government bodies.

constitution-uedca7656ebce71fc34-1.text: 3. Deputies of the State Duma work on a permanent professional basis. They may not be in state service or engage in other paid activities except teaching, scientific and other creative activities.

constitution-ue57fe0cb35b3a02874-1.text: 1. Senators of the Russian Federation and deputies of the State Duma enjoy immunity throughout their terms of office. They may not be detained, arrested or searched except when apprehended at the scene of a crime, nor subjected to a personal inspection except where federal law provides for this to ensure other people's safety.

constitution-u341f60931ba5ae1e2a-1.text: 2. The question of deprivation of immunity is decided by the relevant chamber of the Federal Assembly on the submission of the Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u17838d3aa5f225b9c7-1.text: 1. The Federal Assembly is a permanently functioning body.

constitution-uf7b62993089364f371-1.text: 2. The State Duma meets for its first sitting on the thirtieth day after its election. The President of the Russian Federation may convene a sitting of the State Duma before that date.

constitution-ub25b7362f53c04cbdb-1.text: 3. The first sitting of the State Duma is opened by its oldest deputy.

constitution-u882b4096c7fb90ba7d-1.text: 4. When the State Duma of a new convocation begins work, the powers of the State Duma of the previous convocation cease.

constitution-u85c194901db3a927e0-1.text: 1. The Federation Council and the State Duma meet separately.

constitution-ud9b9b20dd4dbd7bbc2-1.text: 2. Sittings of the Federation Council and the State Duma are open. A chamber may hold closed sittings in cases provided for by its rules of procedure.

constitution-u3b549a82f9c8818a00-1.text: 3. The chambers may meet jointly to hear messages from the President of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u69915e7e94698ad33e-1.text: 1. The Federation Council elects from among its members its Chairman and Deputy Chairmen. The State Duma elects from among its members its Chairman and Deputy Chairmen.

constitution-u743e89cc129400bdd4-1.text: 2. The Chairman and Deputy Chairmen of the Federation Council and the Chairman and Deputy Chairmen of the State Duma preside over sittings and administer the internal proceedings of their chamber.

constitution-u9a4bf8f58c250c4c28-1.text: 3. The Federation Council and the State Duma establish committees and commissions and hold parliamentary hearings on matters within their jurisdiction.

constitution-u549e800ee9a412adbf-1.text: 4. Each chamber adopts its own rules of procedure and decides matters concerning the internal organization of its activities.

constitution-u92d88bf4ef78a58dc2-1.text: 5. To supervise execution of the federal budget, the Federation Council and the State Duma establish the Accounts Chamber, whose composition and operating procedure are determined by federal law.

constitution-u899c795fce952a6fcb-1.text: 1. The Federation Council has jurisdiction over:

constitution-ud89a8a9425ee7ec7d9-1.text: а) approval of changes to boundaries between constituent entities of the Russian Federation;

constitution-uf4cb24344b02183d12-1.text: б) approval of a decree of the President of the Russian Federation introducing martial law;

constitution-ua50438748b9982d335-1.text: в) approval of a decree of the President of the Russian Federation introducing a state of emergency;

constitution-u22800584f1dde4aa57-1.text: г) deciding whether the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation may be used outside the territory of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u6bbde71a6479339565-1.text: д) calling the election of the President of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u2c70763cf425521a05-1.text: е) removal of the President of the Russian Federation from office; deprivation of immunity of a President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers;

constitution-u84e5bc446350e1d2b4-1.text: ж) appointment, on the submission of the President of the Russian Federation, of the Chairman, Deputy Chairman and judges of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation and the Chairman, Deputy Chairmen and judges of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation;

constitution-uabe524a9de9878d6e3-1.text: з) consultations on candidates proposed by the President of the Russian Federation for the offices of Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation, Deputy Prosecutors General of the Russian Federation, prosecutors of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and prosecutors of military and other specialized procuracies equivalent to prosecutors of constituent entities of the Russian Federation;

constitution-uf8e6877345d0f4df75-1.text: и) appointment and removal of the Chairman of the Accounts Chamber and half of its total number of auditors on the submission of the President of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u21b10609fc01ee2578-1.text: к) consultations on candidates proposed by the President of the Russian Federation for heads of federal executive bodies (including federal ministers) responsible for defence, state security, internal affairs, justice, foreign affairs, prevention of emergencies and elimination of the consequences of natural disasters, and public safety;

constitution-u59941df0a28e61e2e2-1.text: л) termination, on the submission of the President of the Russian Federation and in accordance with federal constitutional law, of the powers of the Chairman, Deputy Chairman and judges of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation, the Chairman, Deputy Chairmen and judges of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, and chairmen, deputy chairmen and judges of cassation and appellate courts, if they commit an act disgracing a judge's honour and dignity, or in other cases provided for by federal constitutional law indicating that a judge is unable to exercise their powers;

constitution-u5f35286639858e5821-1.text: м) hearing annual reports of the Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation on the state of legality and law and order in the Russian Federation.

constitution-u1cadaf793f143c6de9-1.text: 2. The Federation Council adopts resolutions on matters assigned to its jurisdiction by the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ub1715308ab9b889cde-1.text: 3. Resolutions of the Federation Council are adopted by a majority of the total number of senators of the Russian Federation, unless the Constitution of the Russian Federation provides for another decision-making procedure.

constitution-u9d4dbf366b62cb64d2-1.text: 1. The State Duma has jurisdiction over:

constitution-u90c038e2536dfea8cd-1.text: а) approval, on the submission of the President of the Russian Federation, of the candidate for Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u981c9746a2e082ccca-1.text: а.1) approval, on the submission of the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, of candidates for Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers, except the federal ministers referred to in point ‘д.1’ of Article 83 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u819198cbfaa5098a51-1.text: б) deciding the question of confidence in the Government of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ud41d6c0909c995ea58-1.text: в) hearing annual reports of the Government of the Russian Federation on the results of its activities, including on questions raised by the State Duma <21>;

constitution-u4d77b53693aa004d5a-1.text: г) appointment and removal of the Chairman of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation;

constitution-uae1e4d08a76f28c4dd-1.text: г.1) hearing annual reports of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u47fd36b5e2de574dd1-1.text: д) appointment and removal of the Deputy Chairman of the Accounts Chamber and half of its total number of auditors on the submission of the President of the Russian Federation;

constitution-uf7fce44b43bee64b13-1.text: е) appointment and removal of the Commissioner for Human Rights, who acts in accordance with federal constitutional law. The Commissioner for Human Rights may be a citizen of the Russian Federation who permanently resides in the Russian Federation and holds neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, the Commissioner for Human Rights is prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u8fcb7b74f865af98bb-1.text: з) bringing charges against the President of the Russian Federation with a view to removal from office or against a President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers with a view to deprivation of immunity.

constitution-u5e30e754e0db63a7e4-1.text: 2. The State Duma adopts resolutions on matters assigned to its jurisdiction by the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ueae0c24de1aa4d95b9-1.text: 3. Resolutions of the State Duma are adopted by a majority of the total number of its deputies, unless the Constitution of the Russian Federation provides for another decision-making procedure.

constitution-u13ea903eee06dd6322-1.text: <21> Part 1 was supplemented with a new point ‘в’, and the letter designations of subsequent points were changed, in accordance with the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 7-ФКЗ of 30 December 2008, ‘On the Supervisory Powers of the State Duma in Relation to the Government of the Russian Federation’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 31 December 2008 (Rossiyskaya Gazeta, 2008, 31 December).

constitution-u2035107b8ec43aeb7b-1.text: The Federation Council and the State Duma are entitled to exercise parliamentary oversight, including sending parliamentary inquiries to heads of state bodies and local self-government bodies on matters within the competence of those bodies and officials. The procedure for parliamentary oversight is determined by federal laws and the rules of procedure of the chambers of the Federal Assembly.

constitution-ucb74e68e4c059d3251-1.text: 1. The right of legislative initiative belongs to the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, senators of the Russian Federation, deputies of the State Duma, the Government of the Russian Federation and legislative (representative) bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation and the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation also have the right of legislative initiative on matters within their jurisdiction.

constitution-u67af0c4e850b10d4c4-1.text: 2. Bills are submitted to the State Duma.

constitution-uade40e8ceec22ceb1a-1.text: 3. Bills on the introduction or abolition of taxes, exemption from their payment, issuance of state loans, changes to the State's financial obligations, and other bills providing for expenditure covered by the federal budget may be submitted only if accompanied by an opinion of the Government of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ub2b686873fedc40fd2-1.text: 1. Federal laws are adopted by the State Duma.

constitution-u12add1eebd51ed5726-1.text: 2. Federal laws are adopted by a majority of the total number of deputies of the State Duma, unless otherwise provided by the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-uc5b0c7e9cbbffad86b-1.text: 3. Federal laws adopted by the State Duma are submitted to the Federation Council for consideration within five days.

constitution-u3810e66768e26e2bd1-1.text: 4. A federal law is deemed approved by the Federation Council if more than half of the total members of that chamber vote for it, or if the Federation Council does not consider it within fourteen days. If the Federation Council rejects a federal law, the chambers may establish a conciliation commission to resolve the disagreements, after which the federal law is subject to reconsideration by the State Duma.

constitution-ud4ef8d20b98c2ebab6-1.text: 5. If the State Duma disagrees with the Federation Council's decision, the federal law is deemed adopted if, on a repeat vote, at least two-thirds of the total number of deputies of the State Duma vote for it.

constitution-u23812ea58d59a4a9b1-1.text: Federal laws adopted by the State Duma on the following matters are subject to mandatory consideration by the Federation Council:

constitution-u4149ffbd2072db31fe-1.text: в) financial, currency, credit and customs regulation, and currency issuance;

constitution-u0822ece56f9b6de645-1.text: г) ratification and denunciation of international treaties of the Russian Federation;

constitution-uca5d1d94738071c63b-1.text: д) the status and protection of the state border of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u648892459687cd797f-1.text: 1. An adopted federal law is sent to the President of the Russian Federation for signature and promulgation within five days.

constitution-u50eb4ac77f4bf8058e-1.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation signs and promulgates the federal law within fourteen days.

constitution-u274b0170005c8155b7-1.text: 3. If the President of the Russian Federation rejects a federal law within fourteen days of its receipt, the State Duma and the Federation Council reconsider it in the manner established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation. If, on reconsideration, the federal law is approved in its previously adopted wording by a majority of at least two-thirds of the total number of senators of the Russian Federation and deputies of the State Duma, it must be signed by the President of the Russian Federation within seven days and promulgated. If, within that period, the President requests the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation to review the constitutionality of the federal law, the time limit for signing it is suspended while the Constitutional Court considers the request. If the Constitutional Court confirms the constitutionality of the federal law, the President signs it within three days of the Constitutional Court's relevant decision. If the Constitutional Court does not confirm its constitutionality, the President returns it to the State Duma unsigned.

constitution-u008102028992022866-1.text: 1. Federal constitutional laws are adopted on matters provided for by the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u6dadf1d60a0397170a-1.text: 2. A federal constitutional law is deemed adopted if approved by a majority of at least three-quarters of the total number of senators of the Russian Federation and at least two-thirds of the total number of deputies of the State Duma. An adopted federal constitutional law must be signed by the President of the Russian Federation and promulgated within fourteen days. If, within that period, the President requests the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation to review the constitutionality of the federal constitutional law, the time limit for signing it is suspended while the Constitutional Court considers the request. If the Constitutional Court confirms the constitutionality of the federal constitutional law, the President signs it within three days of the Constitutional Court's relevant decision. If the Constitutional Court does not confirm its constitutionality, the President returns it to the State Duma unsigned.

constitution-u40e4e30b608a4fd5bc-1.text: 1. The State Duma may be dissolved by the President of the Russian Federation in the cases provided for by Articles 111, 112 and 117 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ua0851ef337b34957f2-1.text: 2. If the State Duma is dissolved, the President of the Russian Federation sets an election date so that the newly elected State Duma meets no later than four months after the dissolution.

constitution-u1952b48548687e5a5b-1.text: 3. The State Duma may not be dissolved on the grounds provided for by Article 117 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation within a year after its election.

constitution-u0d1907011ecd58ae1b-1.text: 4. The State Duma may not be dissolved from the time it brings a charge against the President of the Russian Federation until the Federation Council adopts the corresponding decision.

constitution-u6067343e18d74c9d54-1.text: 5. The State Duma may not be dissolved while martial law or a state of emergency is in effect throughout the territory of the Russian Federation, or during the six months before the expiry of the President of the Russian Federation's term of office.

constitution-u22b7fe8ddb2af3a029-1.text: CHAPTER 6. GOVERNMENT OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION
constitution-u22b7fe8ddb2af3a029-1.locator: CHAPTER 6. GOVERNMENT OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION

constitution-u5956f62c37b53e85aa-1.text: 1. Executive power in the Russian Federation is exercised by the Government of the Russian Federation under the overall direction of the President of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u0e358d9dcaa63b9966-1.text: 2. The Government of the Russian Federation consists of the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers.

constitution-ue717554c211b758459-1.text: 3. The Government of the Russian Federation directs the activities of federal executive bodies, except those whose activities are directed by the President of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u0e270a1d259baa4d28-1.text: 4. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, a Deputy Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, a federal minister or another head of a federal executive body may be a citizen of the Russian Federation who has reached 30 years of age and holds neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, the Chairman and Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation, federal ministers and other heads of federal executive bodies are prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u7a51cf934e2f70f4ba-1.text: 1. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation is appointed by the President of the Russian Federation after the State Duma approves the candidacy.

constitution-ueafa443876bebd076c-1.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation submits a candidate for Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation to the State Duma no later than two weeks after a newly elected President takes office or after the Government of the Russian Federation resigns, or within one week after the State Duma rejects a candidate for Chairman of the Government, or after the Chairman is removed from office by the President or resigns.

constitution-u4301ce4c70b7167d54-1.text: 3. The State Duma considers the candidate for Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation submitted by the President of the Russian Federation within one week of the submission.

constitution-u92116f4419f7ef943d-1.text: 4. After the State Duma rejects the submitted candidates for Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation three times, the President of the Russian Federation appoints the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation. In that event, the President is entitled to dissolve the State Duma and call new elections.

constitution-u24fbf23e1967bb7c7d-1.text: 1. No later than one week after appointment, the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation submits proposals to the President of the Russian Federation on the structure of federal executive bodies, except where the previous Chairman was removed from office by the President of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u2a38cb00e7379d3d31-1.text: 2. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation submits candidates for Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers to the State Duma for approval (except the federal ministers referred to in point ‘д.1’ of Article 83 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation). The State Duma decides on the submitted candidates no later than one week thereafter.

constitution-ua3d21c9f13e8819aee-1.text: 3. Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers whose candidacies have been approved by the State Duma are appointed by the President of the Russian Federation. The President may not refuse to appoint Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation or federal ministers whose candidacies have been approved by the State Duma.

constitution-uc3e0771c024a688457-1.text: 4. After the State Duma rejects three times candidates for Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation or federal ministers submitted under part 2 of this Article, the President of the Russian Federation may appoint Deputy Chairmen and federal ministers from among the candidates submitted by the Chairman of the Government. If, after the State Duma rejects three times the candidates submitted under part 2 of this Article, more than one-third of the positions of members of the Government of the Russian Federation remain vacant (excluding the federal ministerial positions referred to in point ‘д.1’ of Article 83 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation), the President may dissolve the State Duma and call new elections.

constitution-ucabb014f9ea074737b-1.text: 5. In the case provided for by part 4 of Article 111 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, and where the State Duma is dissolved in accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, the President of the Russian Federation appoints Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers (except those referred to in point ‘д.1’ of Article 83 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation) on the submission of the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u91b2386afa79755c12-1.text: The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation organizes the work of the Government of the Russian Federation in accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, and decrees, executive orders and instructions of the President of the Russian Federation. The Chairman bears personal responsibility to the President of the Russian Federation for the exercise of the powers vested in the Government of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u80b368644f4ac7debd-1.text: 1. The Government of the Russian Federation:

constitution-u3ad0f27c9726c5bb3e-1.text: а) prepares and submits the federal budget to the State Duma and ensures its execution; submits a report on execution of the federal budget to the State Duma; submits annual reports to the State Duma on the results of its activities, including on questions raised by the State Duma <22>;

constitution-u0d6c3d7e09e9277163-1.text: б) ensures the implementation of a unified financial, credit and monetary policy in the Russian Federation;

constitution-u73b36b6c8dd41049d9-1.text: в) ensures the implementation in the Russian Federation of a unified socially oriented state policy in culture, science, education, healthcare, social security, support, strengthening and protection of the family, preservation of traditional family values, and environmental protection;

constitution-u1ac58a0697b5de6561-1.text: в.1) ensures state support for the scientific and technological development of the Russian Federation and the preservation and development of its scientific potential;

constitution-u2a5e96d575e257fc45-1.text: в.2) ensures the functioning of a system of social protection for persons with disabilities based on their full and equal exercise of human and civil rights and freedoms, their social inclusion without any discrimination, the creation of an accessible environment for persons with disabilities, and improvement of their quality of life;

constitution-ubd9a9932fba1401d73-1.text: д) takes measures to ensure national defence and state security and implement the foreign policy of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ua65f9d40298d3f2424-1.text: е) takes measures to ensure legality and citizens' rights and freedoms, protect property and public order, and combat crime;

constitution-u28c87aa0c078af8f02-1.text: е.1) takes measures to support civil society institutions, including nonprofit organizations, and ensures their participation in developing and implementing state policy;

constitution-u5cb490c53f7e5808f2-1.text: е.2) takes measures to support voluntary (volunteer) activity;

constitution-u41631c0eb2e3a66a47-1.text: е.3) promotes entrepreneurship and private initiative;

constitution-u3be0fc2e54dfa39122-1.text: е.4) ensures implementation of the principles of social partnership in regulating labour relations and other relations directly connected with them;

constitution-ub67ccac7471625936c-1.text: е.5) takes measures aimed at creating favourable living conditions for the population, reducing the negative environmental impact of economic and other activities, preserving the country's unique natural and biological diversity, and fostering a responsible attitude towards animals in society;

constitution-u868785d980b78c31c9-1.text: е.6) creates conditions for developing a system of environmental education for citizens and fostering environmental awareness and culture;

constitution-uba00074f62741e48c4-1.text: ж) exercises other powers vested in it by the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws and decrees of the President of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ud4ab4661b06aa53718-1.text: 2. The operating procedure of the Government of the Russian Federation is determined by federal constitutional law.

constitution-u356b40e611f4b6edee-1.text: <22> Point ‘а’ of part 1 is reproduced as amended by the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 7-ФКЗ of 30 December 2008, ‘On the Supervisory Powers of the State Duma in Relation to the Government of the Russian Federation’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 31 December 2008 (Rossiyskaya Gazeta, 2008, 31 December).

constitution-ueec2e3b8744b8d1336-1.text: 1. On the basis of and in implementation of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws and decrees, executive orders and instructions of the President of the Russian Federation, the Government of the Russian Federation issues resolutions and executive orders and ensures their implementation.

constitution-u492d40569881c5af5b-1.text: 2. Resolutions and executive orders of the Government of the Russian Federation are binding in the Russian Federation.

constitution-u52d11884dd7e36d50a-1.text: 3. Resolutions and executive orders of the Government of the Russian Federation may be repealed by the President of the Russian Federation if they contradict the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, or decrees and executive orders of the President of the Russian Federation.

constitution-uc19254942079123f45-1.text: The Government of the Russian Federation relinquishes its powers before the newly elected President of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ubcf6acd8a889815198-1.text: 1. The Government of the Russian Federation may tender its resignation, which the President of the Russian Federation accepts or rejects.

constitution-ua8044a241c3c565082-1.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation may decide that the Government of the Russian Federation shall resign.

constitution-uf43d0cbfef1d3de55e-1.text: 3. The State Duma may express no confidence in the Government of the Russian Federation. A resolution of no confidence is adopted by a majority of the total number of deputies of the State Duma. After the State Duma expresses no confidence, the President of the Russian Federation may announce the Government's resignation or disagree with the State Duma's decision. If the State Duma again expresses no confidence in the Government of the Russian Federation within three months, the President announces the Government's resignation or dissolves the State Duma and calls new elections.

constitution-u971ffe1d0975c2336f-1.text: 4. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation may put the question of confidence in the Government to the State Duma, which must consider it within seven days. If the State Duma refuses confidence, the President of the Russian Federation may, within seven days, decide on the Government's resignation or on dissolution of the State Duma and the calling of new elections. If the Government of the Russian Federation again puts the question of confidence to the State Duma within three months and the State Duma refuses confidence, the President decides on the Government's resignation or on dissolution of the State Duma and the calling of new elections.

constitution-u21a89d8a60ff170138-1.text: 4.1. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, a Deputy Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation or a federal minister may tender their resignation, which the President of the Russian Federation accepts or rejects.

constitution-u04e08662211e7ada69-1.text: 5. In the event of resignation or relinquishment of powers, the Government of the Russian Federation continues to act on the instructions of the President of the Russian Federation until a new Government is formed. If the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, a Deputy Chairman or a federal minister is removed from office by the President or resigns, the President may instruct that person to continue performing the duties of the office or assign those duties to another person until the corresponding appointment is made.

constitution-u600612fc524969307d-1.text: 6. The State Duma may not express no confidence in the Government of the Russian Federation, and the Chairman of the Government may not put the question of confidence in the Government to the State Duma, in the cases provided for by parts 3–5 of Article 109 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, or within one year after the Chairman of the Government is appointed in accordance with part 4 of Article 111 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-ub3655bab2470939c6d-1.text: Chapter 7. Judicial power and the procuracy
constitution-ub3655bab2470939c6d-1.locator: Chapter 7. Judicial power and the procuracy

constitution-u10912b0f205f3dd457-1.text: CHAPTER 7. JUDICIAL POWER AND THE PROCURACY <23>
constitution-u10912b0f205f3dd457-1.locator: CHAPTER 7. JUDICIAL POWER AND THE PROCURACY <23>

constitution-u552cc24d616a2fe1bd-1.text: <23> The title of chapter 7 is reproduced as amended by the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 2-ФКЗ of 5 February 2014, ‘On the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation and the Procuracy of the Russian Federation’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 6 February 2014 (Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (www.pravo.gov.ru), 2014, 6 February, No. 0001201402060001).
constitution-u552cc24d616a2fe1bd-1.locator: CHAPTER 7. JUDICIAL POWER AND THE PROCURACY <23>

constitution-u983cc498cc71cab6ae-1.text: 1. Justice in the Russian Federation is administered only by courts.

constitution-ucfc724cfb0067ea3dd-1.text: 2. Judicial power is exercised through constitutional, civil, commercial (arbitrazh), administrative and criminal proceedings.

constitution-ub8bb399c5dbf0847e0-1.text: 3. The judicial system of the Russian Federation is established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal constitutional law. It consists of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation, the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, federal courts of general jurisdiction, commercial (arbitrazh) courts and justices of the peace of constituent entities of the Russian Federation. Extraordinary courts may not be established.

constitution-ua3f1ec3752bc31a200-1.text: Judges may be citizens of the Russian Federation who have reached 25 years of age, have a higher legal education and at least five years' experience in the legal profession, permanently reside in the Russian Federation and hold neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, judges of courts of the Russian Federation are prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation. Federal law may establish additional requirements for judges of courts of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u03955e4dac75a07fb8-1.text: 1. Judges are independent and are subject only to the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal law.

constitution-u569d78416652972bb2-1.text: 2. A court that finds, when considering a case, that an act of a state or other body does not conform to law makes its decision in accordance with the law.

constitution-u621b3f014a9fc1b908-1.text: 2. A judge's powers may be terminated or suspended only in the manner and on the grounds established by federal law.

constitution-u258cc12853705b8813-1.text: 2. A judge may be held criminally liable only in the manner determined by federal law.

constitution-uf29473f5a230fa2632-1.text: 1. Proceedings in all courts are open. A closed hearing is permitted in cases provided for by federal law.

constitution-u780e39cd6cc1a2e8ed-1.text: 2. Criminal trials in absentia are not permitted except in cases provided for by federal law.

constitution-ua84d016b79ad984154-1.text: 3. Judicial proceedings are conducted on the basis of adversarial procedure and equality of the parties.

constitution-ufc40019aee4fc1fc75-1.text: 4. Judicial proceedings are conducted with the participation of jurors in cases provided for by federal law.

constitution-ub8b19c22007cabc0c6-1.text: Courts are funded solely from the federal budget, and funding must ensure the possibility of full and independent administration of justice in accordance with federal law.

constitution-u2713a0af42d766be10-1.text: 1. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation is the highest judicial body of constitutional review in the Russian Federation, exercising judicial power through constitutional proceedings to protect the foundations of the constitutional order and fundamental human and civil rights and freedoms, and to ensure the supremacy and direct effect of the Constitution of the Russian Federation throughout its territory. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation consists of 11 judges, including its Chairman and Deputy Chairman.

constitution-u8795e1202814af5191-1.text: 2. At the request of the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, the State Duma, one-fifth of the senators of the Russian Federation or deputies of the State Duma, the Government of the Russian Federation, the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, or legislative and executive bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation decides cases concerning the conformity with the Constitution of the Russian Federation of:

constitution-u222d31fc79b4453b42-1.text: а) federal constitutional laws, federal laws, and normative acts of the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, the State Duma and the Government of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u037c86853014588978-1.text: б) constitutions of republics, charters, and laws and other normative acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation issued on matters within the jurisdiction of bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation or the joint jurisdiction of bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities;

constitution-u7927d39aeaed5a0430-1.text: в) treaties between bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities, and treaties between bodies of state authority of constituent entities of the Russian Federation;

constitution-uac822c5900d9b4a94b-1.text: г) international treaties of the Russian Federation that have not entered into force.

constitution-u9ecfedc1d99e565a0e-1.text: 3. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation resolves disputes over competence:

constitution-ud556608cb28a54e1db-1.text: а) between federal bodies of state authority;

constitution-ud5294969430d45c494-1.text: б) between bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities;

constitution-u428b292dfec77b83a7-1.text: в) between the highest state bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u5031467975ee54b449-1.text: 4. In the manner established by federal constitutional law, the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation reviews:

constitution-u8c948f08acb29d0494-1.text: а) upon complaints alleging violations of citizens' constitutional rights and freedoms, the constitutionality of laws and other normative acts referred to in points ‘а’ and ‘б’ of part 2 of this Article that were applied in a specific case, if all other domestic judicial remedies have been exhausted;

constitution-u43e6872426ff952f5d-1.text: б) upon requests from courts, the constitutionality of laws and other normative acts referred to in points ‘а’ and ‘б’ of part 2 of this Article that are to be applied in a specific case.

constitution-u3244254bd4b50e0962-1.text: 5. At the request of the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, the State Duma, the Government of the Russian Federation or legislative bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation interprets the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u5f9d361831684be145-1.text: 5.1. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation:

constitution-ua2b159bdb25e2d593d-1.text: а) at the request of the President of the Russian Federation, reviews the constitutionality of draft laws of the Russian Federation amending the Constitution of the Russian Federation, draft federal constitutional laws and federal laws, and laws adopted in the manner provided for by parts 2 and 3 of Article 107 and part 2 of Article 108 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation before their signature by the President of the Russian Federation;

constitution-u3cc2e13f392fbdc4fd-1.text: б) in the manner established by federal constitutional law, decides whether decisions of interstate bodies adopted on the basis of provisions of international treaties of the Russian Federation interpreted in a manner contrary to the Constitution of the Russian Federation can be implemented, and whether a decision of a foreign or international (interstate) court or a foreign or international arbitral tribunal imposing obligations on the Russian Federation can be implemented where that decision conflicts with the foundations of the public legal order of the Russian Federation;

constitution-ud712ebd84f4675d994-1.text: в) at the request of the President of the Russian Federation, in the manner established by federal constitutional law, reviews the constitutionality of laws of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation before they are promulgated by its highest official (the head of its highest executive body of state authority).

constitution-u23a2b31e2d2421e118-1.text: 6. Acts or individual provisions thereof declared unconstitutional cease to have effect; international treaties of the Russian Federation that do not conform to the Constitution of the Russian Federation may not be brought into force or applied. Acts or individual provisions thereof declared constitutional in the interpretation given by the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation may not be applied in a different interpretation.

constitution-u91bc29764e6bd46513-1.text: 7. At the request of the Federation Council, the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation gives an opinion on whether the prescribed procedure has been observed in bringing charges of high treason or commission of another serious crime against the President of the Russian Federation or a President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers.

constitution-u912ae8d49270bd9782-1.text: 8. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation exercises other powers established by federal constitutional law.

constitution-uc48fcb116bcbbc70ba-1.text: The Supreme Court of the Russian Federation is the highest judicial body for civil cases, resolution of economic disputes, criminal, administrative and other cases within the jurisdiction of courts of general jurisdiction and commercial (arbitrazh) courts established in accordance with federal constitutional law and exercising judicial power through civil, commercial (arbitrazh), administrative and criminal proceedings. The Supreme Court of the Russian Federation exercises judicial supervision over the activities of courts of general jurisdiction and commercial (arbitrazh) courts in the procedural forms provided for by federal law and provides explanations on issues of judicial practice.

constitution-u7ba18747bb8eb0a588-1.text: Deleted by an amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation (Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation ‘On the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation and the Procuracy of the Russian Federation’) <24>.

constitution-ua37f029e56f9adaf57-1.text: <24> Article 127 was deleted in accordance with the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 2-ФКЗ of 5 February 2014, ‘On the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation and the Procuracy of the Russian Federation’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 6 February 2014 (Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (www.pravo.gov.ru), 2014, 6 February, No. 0001201402060001).

constitution-u4319e9280f3d61dde6-1.text: 1. The Chairman, Deputy Chairman and judges of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation and the Chairman, Deputy Chairmen and judges of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation are appointed by the Federation Council on the submission of the President of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u010e866f5fba40f497-1.text: 2. Chairmen, deputy chairmen and judges of other federal courts are appointed by the President of the Russian Federation in the manner established by federal constitutional law.

constitution-ua79b16122cf94a13c0-1.text: 3. The powers and the procedure for formation and operation of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation, the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation and other federal courts are established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal constitutional law. The conduct of civil, commercial (arbitrazh), administrative and criminal proceedings is also regulated by the relevant procedural legislation.

constitution-u3fce4370306d35697b-1.text: 1. The Procuracy of the Russian Federation is a unified federal centralized system of bodies supervising observance of the Constitution of the Russian Federation and implementation of laws, supervising observance of human and civil rights and freedoms, conducting criminal prosecution within their powers, and performing other functions. The powers and functions of the Procuracy of the Russian Federation, its organization and operating procedure are determined by federal law.

constitution-u5798d26c2d8e787ef3-1.text: 2. Prosecutors may be citizens of the Russian Federation who hold neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, prosecutors are prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u4f5a406ed5d12890fe-1.text: 3. The Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation and Deputy Prosecutors General are appointed by the President of the Russian Federation after consultations with the Federation Council and are removed from office by the President.

constitution-u9e95d5ee7246a4b138-1.text: 4. Prosecutors of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and prosecutors of military and other specialized procuracies equivalent to prosecutors of constituent entities are appointed by the President of the Russian Federation after consultations with the Federation Council and are removed from office by the President.

constitution-u76bf7e2398a6510079-1.text: 5. Other prosecutors may be appointed and removed from office by the President of the Russian Federation if federal law establishes this procedure for appointment and removal.

constitution-u6e5363e340d876c848-1.text: 6. Unless otherwise provided by federal law, prosecutors of cities and districts and equivalent prosecutors are appointed and removed from office by the Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u4b429f90dfd4c2da0f-1.text: 1. Local self-government in the Russian Federation ensures that the population independently resolves matters of local significance and possesses, uses and disposes of municipal property.

constitution-uf86f431bc872015430-1.text: 2. Local self-government is exercised by citizens through referendums, elections and other forms of direct expression of their will, and through elected and other local self-government bodies.

constitution-ue0fcc46ad47e4cecfb-1.text: 1. Local self-government is exercised in municipal entities whose types are established by federal law. The territories of municipal entities are determined with regard to historical and other local traditions. The structure of local self-government bodies is determined independently by the population in accordance with the general principles of organizing local self-government in the Russian Federation established by federal law.

constitution-u6c7ebb919577ed1da5-1.text: 1.1. Bodies of state authority may participate in forming local self-government bodies and appointing and removing local self-government officials in the manner and cases established by federal law.

constitution-ud4bc181b6e07960c64-1.text: 2. Boundaries of territories within which local self-government is exercised may be changed with regard to the opinion of the population of the relevant territories in the manner established by federal law.

constitution-u865b4591d5084c3b32-1.text: 3. Federal law may establish special features of the exercise of public authority in the territories of cities of federal significance, administrative centres (capitals) of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and other territories.

constitution-ubcb16463a8b870cf06-1.text: 1. Local self-government bodies independently manage municipal property, prepare, approve and execute the local budget, introduce local taxes and levies, resolve other matters of local significance and, in accordance with federal law, ensure access to medical care within their competence.

constitution-u87c8ce50b2768566d2-1.text: 2. Federal law or a law of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation may vest local self-government bodies with specific state powers, provided that the material and financial resources needed to exercise those powers are transferred to them. The exercise of transferred powers is subject to state supervision.

constitution-u3271ae4e7ce2f1d8a9-1.text: 3. Local self-government bodies and bodies of state authority form part of the unified system of public authority in the Russian Federation and cooperate to resolve tasks as effectively as possible in the interests of the population living in the relevant territory.

constitution-ueca6558f745377a4e5-1.text: Local self-government in the Russian Federation is guaranteed by the right to judicial protection and compensation for additional expenditure arising from the performance of public functions by local self-government bodies in cooperation with bodies of state authority, and by a prohibition on restricting the rights of local self-government established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal laws.

constitution-u5a4003294284dbaf1d-1.text: CHAPTER 9. CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS AND REVISION OF THE CONSTITUTION
constitution-u5a4003294284dbaf1d-1.locator: CHAPTER 9. CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS AND REVISION OF THE CONSTITUTION

constitution-ubcd9dd0cb2d0ede7be-1.text: Proposals to amend or revise provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation may be submitted by the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, the State Duma, the Government of the Russian Federation, legislative (representative) bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, and a group comprising at least one-fifth of the members of the Federation Council or deputies of the State Duma.

constitution-u3180bb9392d4626905-1.text: 1. The provisions of chapters 1, 2 and 9 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation may not be revised by the Federal Assembly.

constitution-u16cd3d2b50e7b8648e-1.text: 2. If a proposal to revise the provisions of chapters 1, 2 and 9 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation is supported by votes of three-fifths of the total number of members of the Federation Council and deputies of the State Duma, a Constitutional Assembly is convened in accordance with federal constitutional law.

constitution-u61850e033f833572d9-1.text: 3. The Constitutional Assembly either confirms that the Constitution of the Russian Federation is to remain unchanged or drafts a new Constitution of the Russian Federation, which is adopted by the Constitutional Assembly by two-thirds of the total number of its members or submitted to a popular vote. In a popular vote, the Constitution of the Russian Federation is deemed adopted if more than half of the voters who participated vote for it, provided that more than half of all voters participated.

constitution-u5220059d9850a342bb-1.text: Amendments to chapters 3–8 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation are adopted in the manner provided for the adoption of a federal constitutional law and enter into force after approval by the legislative bodies of at least two-thirds of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u2b8c0ef886e9a7653a-1.text: 1. Amendments to Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, which determines the composition of the Russian Federation, are made on the basis of a federal constitutional law on admission to the Russian Federation and formation within it of a new constituent entity of the Russian Federation, or on a change in the constitutional and legal status of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u6b694052c2a5a8c6a7-1.text: 2. If the name of a republic, territory, region, city of federal significance, autonomous region or autonomous area changes, the new name of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation must be included in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.

constitution-u6ef988dc3224416418-1.text: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
constitution-u6ef988dc3224416418-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-ud3a53595f71c5a15e6-1.text: 1. The Constitution of the Russian Federation enters into force on the date of its official publication following the popular vote.
constitution-ud3a53595f71c5a15e6-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-udaee69a75dcca3619c-1.text: The day of the popular vote, 12 December 1993, is deemed the date of adoption of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
constitution-udaee69a75dcca3619c-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-ueb9efa06ee6448e35c-1.text: At the same time, the Constitution (Fundamental Law) of the Russian Federation — Russia, adopted on 12 April 1978 with subsequent amendments and additions, ceases to have effect.
constitution-ueb9efa06ee6448e35c-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-u84de53f37f2b46fbc8-1.text: If provisions of the Federation Treaty — the Treaty on the Delimitation of Matters of Jurisdiction and Powers between Federal Bodies of State Authority of the Russian Federation and Bodies of State Authority of Sovereign Republics within the Russian Federation; the Treaty on the Delimitation of Matters of Jurisdiction and Powers between Federal Bodies of State Authority of the Russian Federation and Bodies of State Authority of Territories, Regions and the Cities of Moscow and Saint Petersburg of the Russian Federation; and the Treaty on the Delimitation of Matters of Jurisdiction and Powers between Federal Bodies of State Authority of the Russian Federation and Bodies of State Authority of the Autonomous Region and Autonomous Areas within the Russian Federation — or of other treaties between federal bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities, or treaties between bodies of state authority of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, do not conform to provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, the provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation apply.
constitution-u84de53f37f2b46fbc8-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-ud0435594dbab36718a-1.text: 2. Laws and other legal acts in force in the territory of the Russian Federation before this Constitution enters into force apply insofar as they do not contradict the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
constitution-ud0435594dbab36718a-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-u73096f22022b849bf3-1.text: 3. From the day this Constitution enters into force, the President of the Russian Federation elected in accordance with the Constitution (Fundamental Law) of the Russian Federation — Russia exercises the powers established by this Constitution until the expiry of the term for which the President was elected.
constitution-u73096f22022b849bf3-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-u631fb0197a402715a6-1.text: 4. From the day this Constitution enters into force, the Council of Ministers — Government of the Russian Federation acquires the rights, duties and responsibilities of the Government of the Russian Federation established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation, and henceforth is called the Government of the Russian Federation.
constitution-u631fb0197a402715a6-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-u08d6d192027331d10b-1.text: 5. Courts in the Russian Federation administer justice in accordance with their powers established by this Constitution.
constitution-u08d6d192027331d10b-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-uf28b820b0a8482f807-1.text: After the Constitution enters into force, judges of all courts of the Russian Federation retain their powers until the expiry of the terms for which they were elected. Vacant positions are filled in the manner established by this Constitution.
constitution-uf28b820b0a8482f807-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-u37b9edfb2691fc94c2-1.text: 6. Until a federal law establishing the procedure for courts to hear cases with the participation of jurors is brought into effect, the previous procedure for judicial consideration of the relevant cases is retained.
constitution-u37b9edfb2691fc94c2-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-ua18f8051be0115088a-1.text: Until the criminal procedural legislation of the Russian Federation is brought into conformity with the provisions of this Constitution, the previous procedure for arrest, custody and detention of persons suspected of committing crimes is retained.
constitution-ua18f8051be0115088a-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-u6c23d853830a96b159-1.text: 7. The Federation Council of the first convocation and the State Duma of the first convocation are elected for a term of two years.
constitution-u6c23d853830a96b159-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-u8dd88507454fd03808-1.text: 8. The Federation Council meets for its first sitting on the thirtieth day after its election. Its first sitting is opened by the President of the Russian Federation.
constitution-u8dd88507454fd03808-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-ud01b5e710136419417-1.text: 9. A deputy of the State Duma of the first convocation may simultaneously be a member of the Government of the Russian Federation. The provisions of this Constitution on deputies' immunity do not apply to deputies of the State Duma who are members of the Government of the Russian Federation insofar as liability for actions (or inaction) connected with the performance of official duties is concerned.
constitution-ud01b5e710136419417-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

constitution-uc9187d1867aef2ea16-1.text: Deputies of the Federation Council of the first convocation exercise their powers on a non-permanent basis.
constitution-uc9187d1867aef2ea16-1.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
